symbols.name: run
symbols.doc:
Host `build` when the engine started this file; otherwise do nothing.

A build file ends with `run(MyBuild)`. Started by the engine, the file
becomes its worker. Imported, by a test say, the call is a no-op, even
inside a command the engine is running for a body, whose environment still
names the engine. Run by hand with `python`, it says how a build is run
and exits.

packages.name: zuke.tools._tooling
packages.summary: The settings every wrapper's settings extend: `@zuke/core`'s tooling base.

symbols.name: DynamicToolSettings
symbols.doc:
Fluent settings for a defineTool tool: build the argv with
DynamicToolSettings.arg/DynamicToolSettings.flag/DynamicToolSettings.option (in call order), plus all the shared chainers
(`cwd`, `env`, `noThrow`, `quiet`, `toolPath`, `args`).

members.name: arg
members.doc: Append raw positional/argument tokens.

members.name: flag
members.doc: Append a boolean flag, e.g. `flag("verbose")` → `--verbose` (or `-v`).

members.name: option
members.signature: option(name: str, value: str | float) -> Self
members.doc: Append a flag and its value as two tokens, e.g. `--output dist`.

symbols.name: SubcommandSettings
symbols.doc:
Base for a wrapper over a CLI organised into **subcommand groups** — a command
path built with command plus repeatable `--flag [value]` options built
with flag. The agent and cloud wrappers (`gh`, `gcloud`, `claude`,
`gemini`, `codex`) share this shape; each sets its binary via
ToolSettings.defaultTool and, when needed, a fixed prefix via
leadingTokens or between-command global flags via middleTokens.

The argv is assembled as
`[...leadingTokens(), ...command, ...middleTokens(), ...flags]`, keeping every
token a discrete argv entry so command construction stays injection-free.

members.name: command
members.doc: Append command-path tokens — the group, verb, and operands — in order.

members.name: flag
members.signature: flag(name: str, value: str | float | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Add an arbitrary flag. With a value it renders `--name value`; without one
the bare `--name`. Repeatable.

symbols.name: ToolSettings

members.name: env
members.doc: Merge additional environment variables for the process.

members.name: cwd
members.doc: Set the working directory for the process.

members.name: no_throw
members.doc: Do not throw on a non-zero exit; inspect `code` on the output instead.

members.name: quiet
members.doc: Suppress live stdout/stderr streaming to the terminal.

members.name: kill_after
members.doc:
Kill the tool if it runs longer than `ms` milliseconds, raising a
`CommandTimeoutError`. Fires even under noThrow.

members.name: max_captured_bytes
members.doc:
Cap how much of **each** captured stream the run keeps in memory, in bytes
(default 8 MiB). Once the cap is reached the oldest bytes are dropped,
`CommandOutput.truncated` is set, and `CommandOutput.text` prefixes a
notice. Raise it for a tool whose whole output must be parsed — a coverage
report, a `--json` dump — and lower it to bound a chatty one. Live
streaming to the terminal is never capped.

members.name: tool_path
members.doc: Override the binary to run (e.g. an absolute path to the tool).

members.name: from_node_modules
members.doc:
Resolve the binary npx-style: walk up from the working directory looking
for `node_modules/.bin/<tool>`, falling back to `PATH` on a miss. Overrides
both the wrapper default and the ambient `ZUKE_TOOL_RESOLUTION`. Has no
effect once toolPath is set (an explicit path always wins).

members.name: from_path
members.doc: Resolve the binary from `PATH` only, ignoring any `node_modules/.bin`.

members.name: args
members.doc: Escape hatch: append raw arguments after all typed options.

symbols.doc: Typed task functions over the reviewers, for a build that calls rather than declares them.

members.name: review
members.signature: static async review(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[ReviewSettings], ReviewSettings]) -> None
members.doc:
Run the configured reviewers as peers of one target, in order. Throws when
a reviewer's gate trips, as the target it guards would fail.

members.name: preflight
members.signature: static async preflight(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[ReviewSettings], ReviewSettings]) -> None
members.doc:
Run the reviewers' preflight: on a comment-started run, refuse a commenter

symbols.name: DiffSettings
symbols.doc: Fluent diff source configuration passed to "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.diff.

members.name: base
members.doc: Review the diff against `ref` (e.g. `"origin/main"`).

members.name: staged
members.doc: Review the staged changes (`git diff --cached`).

members.name: text
members.doc: Review a diff supplied directly, bypassing `git` (useful in tests).

members.name: fetch_base
members.signature: fetch_base(branch: str | None=None, remote: str | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Fetch the base branch (a shallow, tag-less `git fetch`) before diffing, and
diff against it — so CI needs no manual `git fetch` step. With no `branch`,
the base is auto-detected from the CI environment (GitHub's `GITHUB_BASE_REF`
— the pull request's base branch). Honoured by the "./fixer.ts".AiFixer; if the fetch fails it falls back to the working-tree
diff.

symbols.name: DiscussionSettings
symbols.doc:
Fluent settings for "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.discussion — who the
reviewer listens to on the PR thread, and how much of it the model may see.

members.name: trust_associations
members.doc:
Replace the trusted `author_association` set (default `OWNER`, `MEMBER`,
`COLLABORATOR`). Comments from authors outside it (and outside
trustAuthors) are dropped before the model sees them.

members.name: trust_authors
members.doc:
Trust these author logins in addition to the association rule — e.g. an
outside collaborator whose review the project wants the reviewer to
engage with.

members.name: max_comment_tokens
members.doc:
Cap the total comment text sent to the model at roughly this many tokens
(default 4000), newest comments kept first — so a wall of text cannot
crowd the diff and the rubric out of the context window.

members.name: threads
members.doc:
Also anchor each finding to a file/line **review thread** on the pull
request, so a maintainer contests it by replying in that thread instead of
quoting its id somewhere on the PR.

The summary comment is posted either way and stays the one source of
truth: it lists every finding — anchored or not — and carries the state
block, so a thread that cannot be posted never hides a finding. The
reviewer replies into the thread with the outcome and resolves it once the
finding is fixed or dismissed. GitHub only; on other hosts the reviewer
notes that and posts the summary alone.

members.name: commands
members.doc:
Take commands from maintainers, addressed to `mention` — e.g.
`"@zuke-build"`, the account the workflow's comment command is addressed
to, so one handle serves both.

With it set, every review comment carries a collapsed **Commands** panel
listing what a maintainer can say, and a trusted comment starting with
`<mention> accept <id> <reason>` **accepts** the finding: it is recorded as
accepted for this pull request without adjudication, answered in its
thread and the thread resolved, and never re-raised on the pull request
by any reviewer, however it is reworded, moved or escalated. In a
finding's own thread the id may be left out. The trust gate is the one
rebuttals pass — trustAssociations and trustAuthors,
decided in code from the host's author metadata — so a stranger's
`accept` is dropped before anything reads it. Unlike a rebuttal, an
acceptance is **one key**: no adjudicator weighs it. On a host where the
default associations admit accounts that should not decide for the
project (GitHub's `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR` include read-only ones),
narrow the gate with trustAssociations or trustAuthors
before turning commands on.

The panel also lists `<mention> review`, the workflow's comment command
that runs the review on demand; pair this with `aiReviewWorkflow`'s
`command` so that both are true.

members.name: score_above
members.doc: Fail when the assessed risk score is strictly above `value` (0–10).

members.name: severity_at_least
members.doc: Fail when the overall severity is at least `value`.

symbols.name: Reviewer
symbols.doc:
A fluent AI reviewer. Construct one via securityReviewer (and the
sibling factories), configure it, and attach it to a target with
`.validateBefore(...)` / `.validateAfter(...)`. `.provider(...)` and
`.apiKey(...)` are required; everything else has a default.

members.name: provider
members.doc: Set the model provider (required).

members.name: api_key
members.doc: Set the API key, from a secret parameter or a literal string (required).

members.name: model
members.doc: Override the model (default: the provider's recommended model).

members.name: effort
members.doc: Set the thinking-effort hint (honoured by Claude; ignored elsewhere).

members.name: criteria
members.doc:
Optional project-specific notes appended above the diff in the user prompt
— framing that fine-tunes the built-in rubric (e.g. "strict TypeScript,
no `any`/`as`"). Works for every reviewer; the assessment's own system
prompt already covers what to look for, so this is purely additive.

These notes are **read from the head under review**, and cannot be
anything else: they are build code, evaluated by the very build the
pull request changed, so there is no base copy to read short of running
the base's build. A branch can therefore widen what its own review
overlooks, which is real but bounded — the change is first-party code in
the diff a maintainer reads, and a build that could not configure its own
reviewer from its own source would be a different feature.
Reviewer.criteriaFile is the base-anchored form for notes that
should not be editable by the change they judge.

members.name: diff
members.doc: Configure the diff source (default: the working-tree diff, `git diff`).

members.name: include
members.doc: Only review files matching these globs (default: all files).

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Exclude files matching these globs (in addition to lockfiles).

members.name: max_diff_tokens
members.doc: Cap the diff at roughly this many tokens, truncating the rest.

members.name: fail_when
members.doc: Choose the gate that breaks the build (default: score above 7).

members.name: on_error
members.doc:
What to do when the review itself fails (API error, refusal, bad JSON):
`"fail"` breaks the build (default), `"warn"` logs and passes.

members.name: skip_if_key_missing
members.doc:
Skip the review (instead of failing) when the API key is missing — handy
when the key is a CI-only secret. The skip is announced on the console and
in the job summary so the gap is visible.

members.name: comment
members.doc:
Also post the review to the pull/merge request as a comment. Works on
every supported CI host — GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines,
Bitbucket Pipelines — dispatched at runtime by detectCiHost. A
no-op outside a PR context (e.g. local runs). On each host the workflow
must grant the right scope: GitHub `pull-requests: write`, GitLab a token
with the `api` scope, Azure `System.AccessToken`, Bitbucket an app
password.

`mode` chooses how re-runs post: `"update"` (default) keeps a single
comment per reviewer, edited in place; `"append"` posts a fresh comment
every run, so earlier assessments — and their finding ids — stay on the
thread as history. The discussion feature works with both: its state block
rides on every comment, and the newest one is read back.

Reviewers attached side by side to one target —
`.validateBefore(security, quality)` — post **one** comment between them
rather than one each: a table of every reviewer's verdict, the findings of
all of them in one table with a column naming the reviewer (and its
badge) that raised each, and each reviewer's full report folded
underneath. Every one of them runs even when an earlier one fails its
gate; the target then fails with all of their reasons. The comment is
posted by the last of them, with its token, and appended when any of
them appends. Each reviewer's discussion state rides in it under the
reviewer's name, and a reviewer that used to post alone still reads its
old comment. Another validation between two reviewers splits them, and a
reviewer alone posts its own comment as before.

members.name: comment_token
members.doc:
The token used to post the PR/MR comment. Defaults to the active host's
conventional env var: `GITHUB_TOKEN` (GitHub), `GITLAB_TOKEN` (GitLab),
`SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` (Azure), `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` (Bitbucket).

A function is called each time a post needs the token — for a token that
does not exist until the build mints it, such as a GitHub App installation
token narrowed to `pull_requests: write`, which makes the comments the
app's rather than `github-actions[bot]`'s. A function that mints should
remember its result, since a review posts more than once. The generated
workflow cannot name a secret for a function, so it passes the host's
default token alongside, for the function to fall back to.

members.name: github_token
members.doc: Backwards-compatible alias for commentToken.

members.name: reactions
members.doc:
Whether the reviewer reacts on the pull request to show its progress (on
by default, whenever `.comment()` is set). On the description: 👀 while
it runs, then 👍 when it passes clean, 🎉 when it passes clean where the
previous run failed, 🤏 when it has findings under the failing threshold
(😕 on GitHub, whose reaction set has no 🤏), 👎 when it fails. On the
comment that started a comment-started run: 👍 as it starts, 😕 when the
run could not review. On a trusted maintainer's reply: 👀 once read, ❤️
when it decided a finding. The reviewers on one pull request share the
reactions, so the verdict shown is the worst of a run's. GitHub and
GitLab have the reactions; on Azure DevOps and Bitbucket this is a no-op.
`false` turns all of it off, as does `.quiet()`, under which the reviewer
does not speak on the pull request.

members.name: badge
members.doc:
The emoji that marks this reviewer's findings — in the combined comment
the reviewers of one target share (see comment), and on the review
threads it opens. Defaults by kind: 🛡️ security, 🧹 code quality
(`genericReviewer`), 🔑 secrets, 🐛 correctness, ⚖️ license. Set one when
two reviewers of a kind review side by side — and give one of them a
name of its own, which is what the comment tells them apart by.

members.name: quiet
members.doc: Suppress the findings printout and the job-summary section.

members.name: conventions_file
members.signature: conventions_file(path: str, max_tokens: float | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Feed the project's conventions document (e.g. `AGENTS.md`) to the model as
reference material, so the review judges the change against the project's
documented rules instead of generic taste. When the diff has a base ref
(`.diff((d) => d.base(...))` or a successful `.fetchBase()`), the file is
read from that **base** via `git show` — never from the head under review,
so a pull request cannot rewrite the rules it is judged by. Without a base
(a local working-tree review) it is read from disk. Truncated at roughly
`maxTokens` (default 8000).

members.name: criteria_file
members.signature: criteria_file(path: str, max_tokens: float | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Project-specific notes read from a **file**, appended to whatever
Reviewer.criteria set inline — the base-anchored half of the same
slot.

Read exactly as Reviewer.conventionsFile is: from the diff's base
ref via `git show` when there is one, from disk otherwise, truncated at
roughly `maxTokens` (default 8000). That is the point of it. A note that
tells the reviewer a design is accepted — and so suppresses the findings
that restate it — is a rule the review is judged by, and a pull request
should not be able to add one to its own run. Keeping it in a file the
base supplies costs one merge of lag, which is the same lag the
conventions document already accepts, and is arguably the point: a newly
accepted design should be agreed before it starts muting findings.

Use it for what a branch should not be able to widen; keep
Reviewer.criteria for the framing that travels with the build.

What it does not buy: the build still decides *whether* to read a criteria
document at all, and that decision is head code, so a branch can drop the
call as easily as it can edit a string. This bounds what a change can add
to the rules of its own review, not whether the reviewer is configured —
the same limit Reviewer.conventionsFile has, and the reason the
diff a maintainer reads remains the control that matters.

members.name: file_context
members.doc:
Also send the full post-image contents of the changed files (read via
`git show HEAD:<path>`), bounded at roughly `maxTokens` (default 12000) —
so the model can check a finding against the surrounding code (an existing
guard, a validation a few lines away) instead of judging hunks in
isolation. Skipped silently for a literal `.diff((d) => d.text(...))`
source with no repository behind it.

members.name: verify
members.doc:
Add an adversarial verification pass: after the review produces candidate
findings, a second model call re-checks each against the diff (and the
fileContext, when enabled) and refutes any whose failure path it
cannot concretely trace. Refuted candidates are listed in the report but
neither posted as findings nor gated on. Costs one extra API call per
review with findings; if the pass itself errors, the unverified findings
are kept (fail toward reporting, never toward silence).

members.name: discussion
members.doc:
Engage with the pull-request discussion instead of repeating findings: the
reviewer reads the PR's comments, and when a **trusted** commenter (by the
host's own author metadata — see DiscussionSettings) contests a
finding by quoting its ID, an adjudication pass weighs the rebuttal on
technical merit and either upholds the finding (with the gap named) or
dismisses it. Dismissals persist across runs in a state block inside the
reviewer's own PR comment, so a dismissed finding — or a rewording of it —
does not resurface without new evidence. Requires comment (the
comment is where state lives) and a host that can list comments (GitHub
currently); elsewhere the discussion is skipped with a console note.

Untrusted comments are dropped in code before any prompt is built — the
model never sees them, so a drive-by "the maintainer approved this"
comment cannot influence the review.

symbols.name: ReviewSettings
symbols.doc:
The reviewers one `AiTasks.review` runs, as `.validateBefore(a, b)` would
run them, and the target they review for.

members.name: target
members.doc: The target the reviewers are attached to, named in their output; `review` by default.

members.name: generic
members.doc: Add a code-quality reviewer, as genericReviewer makes it.

members.name: security
members.doc: Add a security reviewer, as securityReviewer makes it.

members.name: secrets
members.doc: Add a leaked-secrets reviewer, as secretsReviewer makes it.

members.name: correctness
members.doc: Add a correctness reviewer, as correctnessReviewer makes it.

members.name: license
members.doc: Add a license reviewer, as licenseReviewer makes it.

packages.name: zuke.tools.apple
packages.summary: `@zuke/apple` 1.1.0: `@zuke/apple` — typed task wrappers for Apple's code-signing tools in Zuke builds: `codesign`, `xcrun notarytool`, `security` and `ditto`.

members.name: file
members.doc: The `.ipa` or `.pkg` to upload or validate (`--file`); required.

members.name: type_
members.doc: The app's platform (`--type`); required.

members.name: api_key
members.doc:
Authenticate with an App Store Connect API key: its key id and issuer id
(`--apiKey`, `--apiIssuer`). `altool` finds `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8` in
`~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys` and its other search directories, or in
apiPrivateKeysDir.

members.name: api_private_keys_dir
members.doc:
The directory holding `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8`, passed to `altool` as
`API_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR`.

members.name: apple_id
members.doc:
Authenticate with an Apple ID and an app-specific password
(`--username`, `--password`). The password is handed to `altool` in an
environment variable it reads through `@env:`, so it is never on the
command line, and it is registered with the run's redactor.

members.name: upload_app
members.signature: static async upload_app(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[AltoolSettings], AltoolSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Upload an app to App Store Connect: `xcrun altool --upload-app`.

members.name: validate_app
members.signature: static async validate_app(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[AltoolSettings], AltoolSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Validate an app without uploading it: `xcrun altool --validate-app`.

symbols.name: AppStoreConnectSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for a task that calls the App Store Connect API with an API key
(*Users and Access → Integrations* in App Store Connect): the issuer id, the
key id, and the `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8` private key.

The private key and every token signed with it stay out of progress lines
and errors. Declare them in the build as `parameter(...).secret()` so Zuke
masks them in its own output too.

members.name: issuer_id
members.doc: The API key's issuer id, a UUID.

members.name: key_id
members.doc: The API key's id, e.g. `ABC123`.

members.name: private_key
members.doc: The private key, as the PEM text of `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8`.

members.name: private_key_file
members.doc: Read the private key from `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8`.

members.name: api_url
members.doc:
The API's base URL, `https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com` by default.
It carries the token, so it must be `https:` unless it is loopback or
`ZUKE_ALLOW_INSECURE_URL` is set.

symbols.name: CodesignSettings
symbols.doc:
The shared shape of every `codesign` operation: the files it acts on and how
verbose it is. Each operation subclass names its mode flag and its own
options.

members.name: file
members.doc:
The code to act on (positional) — an app bundle, framework, binary or
disk image; repeatable. A relative path starting with `-` is passed as
`./-…` so `codesign` cannot read it as an option.

members.name: verbose
members.doc:
More output (`--verbose`, or `--verbose=<level>` with a level). `display`
shows more of the signature at each level; `4` lists everything.

members.name: identity
members.doc:
The signing identity (`--sign <identity>`): a certificate's common name,
a substring of it, or its SHA-1 hash. `-` signs ad hoc. Required.

members.name: force
members.doc: Replace an existing signature (`--force`).

members.name: deep
members.doc: Sign nested code as well (`--deep`). Apple discourages it for signing.

members.name: options
members.doc:
Signature option flags (`--options`, comma-joined); repeatable.
`runtime` enables the hardened runtime notarization requires.

members.name: timestamp
members.doc:
Request a secure timestamp (`--timestamp`), from `url` when given
(`--timestamp=<url>`). Notarization requires one.

members.name: entitlements
members.doc: The entitlements plist to embed (`--entitlements`).

members.name: keychain
members.doc: Look the identity up in this keychain only (`--keychain`).

members.name: identifier
members.doc: The code's identifier (`--identifier`), overriding the bundle id.

members.name: sign
members.signature: static async sign(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[CodesignSignSettings], CodesignSignSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Sign code with `codesign --sign`.

members.name: verify
members.signature: static async verify(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[CodesignVerifySettings], CodesignVerifySettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Check a signature with `codesign --verify`; a bad one fails the run.

members.name: display
members.signature: static async display(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[CodesignDisplaySettings], CodesignDisplaySettings]) -> object
members.doc:
Describe a signature with `codesign --display`. `codesign` prints the
description on **stderr**, so it is returned parsed, with the raw text and
the command output alongside.

members.name: strict
members.doc: Apply the strict validation rules notarization uses (`--strict`).

members.name: deep
members.doc: Verify nested code as well (`--deep`).

members.name: create
members.doc: Create an archive rather than copy (`-c`).

members.name: extract
members.doc: Extract an archive rather than copy (`-x`).

members.name: pkzip
members.doc: Use the PKZip format for the archive (`-k`) instead of CPIO.

members.name: sequester_rsrc
members.doc:
Keep resource forks and HFS metadata in a `__MACOSX` directory inside the
archive (`--sequesterRsrc`), the way the Finder's own compress does.

members.name: keep_parent
members.doc:
Put the source directory itself in the archive, not only its contents
(`--keepParent`) — what makes a zipped `MyApp.app` unzip as `MyApp.app`.

members.name: source
members.doc: What to copy or archive (positional). Required.

members.name: destination
members.doc: Where to write it (positional). Required.

members.name: copy
members.signature: static async copy(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[DittoSettings], DittoSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Copy a file or directory tree with `ditto`, metadata intact.

members.name: archive
members.signature: static async archive(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[DittoSettings], DittoSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Write a zip archive: `ditto -c -k`, then the lambda's settings.

members.name: extract
members.signature: static async extract(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[DittoSettings], DittoSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Unpack a zip archive: `ditto -x -k`, then the lambda's settings.

members.name: method
members.doc: How the archive is exported (`method`); required.

members.name: team_id
members.doc: The developer team id (`teamID`).

members.name: signing_style
members.doc: Automatic or manual signing (`signingStyle`).

members.name: signing_certificate
members.doc: The certificate to sign with, e.g. `Apple Distribution` (`signingCertificate`).

members.name: provisioning_profile
members.doc:
The provisioning profile, by name or UUID, for one bundle identifier
(`provisioningProfiles`); repeatable, once per app and extension.

members.name: destination
members.doc: Export to a directory, or upload to App Store Connect (`destination`).

members.name: upload_symbols
members.doc: Include symbols for crash reports (`uploadSymbols`).

members.name: manage_app_version_and_build_number
members.doc: Let App Store Connect manage the version and build number (`manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber`).

members.name: strip_swift_symbols
members.doc: Strip Swift symbols from the binary (`stripSwiftSymbols`).

members.name: test_flight_internal_testing_only
members.doc: Limit a TestFlight upload to internal testers (`testFlightInternalTestingOnly`).

members.name: submission_id
members.doc: The submission to describe (positional). Required.

members.name: submission_id
members.doc: The submission whose log to fetch (positional). Required.

symbols.name: NotarytoolSettings
symbols.doc:
The shared settings of every `xcrun notarytool` subcommand: the credentials,
and the masking of the app-specific password. A subclass names its
subcommand and builds its own arguments.

members.name: key
members.doc: The App Store Connect API private key file, `AuthKey_<id>.p8` (`--key`).

members.name: key_id
members.doc: The API key's id (`--key-id`).

members.name: issuer
members.doc: The API key's issuer UUID (`--issuer`); omit it for an individual key.

members.name: keychain_profile
members.doc:
Authenticate with credentials saved by `notarytool store-credentials`
(`--keychain-profile`).

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain to read the keychainProfile from (`--keychain`).

members.name: apple_id
members.doc: The Apple ID to authenticate as (`--apple-id`).

members.name: password
members.doc:
The Apple ID's app-specific password (`--password`). Registered with the
run's redactor and masked out of any error this run raises.

members.name: team_id
members.doc: The developer team id the Apple ID signs for (`--team-id`).

members.name: tool_path
members.doc: Override the binary, remembered so a follow-up command uses it too.

members.name: env
members.doc: Merge environment variables, remembered for a follow-up command too.

members.name: cwd
members.doc: Set the working directory, remembered for a follow-up command too.

members.name: file
members.doc: The archive to notarize — a `.zip`, `.pkg` or `.dmg` (positional). Required.

members.name: wait
members.doc:
Wait for Apple to finish processing (`--wait`). With it the result
carries the final status, and `NotarytoolTasks.submit` throws a
`NotarizationError` for anything but `Accepted`.

members.name: timeout
members.doc: How long `--wait` waits, e.g. `30m` or `1h` (`--timeout`). Needs wait.

members.name: log_for
members.doc:
Settings for `notarytool log <id>` that reuse this submission's
credentials, binary, environment and working directory.

members.name: submit
members.signature: static async submit(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[NotarytoolSubmitSettings], NotarytoolSubmitSettings]) -> object
members.doc:
Upload an archive with `notarytool submit` and return the parsed result.
With `.wait()`, a final status other than `Accepted` fetches the
submission's log and throws a NotarizationError listing its
issues — unless `.noThrow()` was set, when the result is returned for the
caller to inspect.

members.name: info
members.signature: static async info(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[NotarytoolInfoSettings], NotarytoolInfoSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read a submission's status with `notarytool info`.

members.name: log
members.signature: static async log(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[NotarytoolLogSettings], NotarytoolLogSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Fetch and parse a submission's notarization log with `notarytool log`.

members.name: history
members.signature: static async history(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[NotarytoolHistorySettings], NotarytoolHistorySettings]) -> object
members.doc: List the team's past submissions with `notarytool history`.

members.name: file
members.doc: Read the profile from a `.mobileprovision` file.

members.name: base64
members.doc:
Take the profile as base64 — how a CI secret usually holds it
(`base64 -i profile.mobileprovision`).

members.name: directory
members.doc: Install into this directory instead of Xcode's two defaults; repeatable.

members.name: allow_expired
members.doc: Install the profile even if it has expired.

members.name: inspect
members.signature: static async inspect(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[ProvisioningProfileSettings], ProvisioningProfileSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read what a profile says about itself, without installing it.

members.name: install
members.signature: static async install(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[ProvisioningProfileSettings], ProvisioningProfileSettings]) -> object
members.doc:
Install a profile where Xcode looks for it, named by its UUID. Refuses an
expired profile unless `.allowExpired()`.

members.name: password
members.doc:
The new keychain's password (`-p`). A secret: masked in every rendering
of the command. Without it `security` prompts for one.

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain(s) to create (positional); repeatable. Required.

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain(s) to delete (positional); repeatable. Required.

members.name: policy
members.doc: Only identities usable under this policy (`-p`), e.g. `codesigning`.

members.name: search
members.doc: Only identities whose name contains this string (`-s`).

members.name: valid
members.doc: Only valid identities (`-v`) — not expired, revoked or untrusted.

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain(s) to search (positional); the search list when omitted.

members.name: file
members.doc: The file to import, e.g. a `.p12` (positional). Required.

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain to import into (`-k`); the default keychain when omitted.

members.name: passphrase
members.doc:
The file's passphrase (`-P`), e.g. a `.p12`'s export password. A secret:
masked in every rendering of the command.

members.name: application
members.doc:
An application allowed to use the imported key without a prompt (`-T`),
e.g. `/usr/bin/codesign`; repeatable.

members.name: type_
members.doc: The type of item in the file (`-t`).

members.name: format
members.doc: The file's format (`-f`), e.g. `pkcs12`.

members.name: non_extractable
members.doc: Make the imported private key non-extractable (`-x`).

members.name: domain
members.doc: The preference domain to read or set (`-d`).

members.name: set
members.doc:
Replace the search list with these keychains (`-s`), in order. Called
with none, it empties the list. Repeat calls append.

symbols.name: SecuritySetKeychainSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `security set-keychain-settings`. With no flags, the keychain
never locks on its own — no timeout, and no lock on sleep — which is what a
CI keychain wants for the length of a build.

members.name: lock_on_sleep
members.doc: Lock the keychain when the machine sleeps (`-l`).

members.name: lock_after_timeout
members.doc: Lock the keychain after timeout seconds of inactivity (`-u`).

members.name: timeout
members.doc: The inactivity timeout, in seconds (`-t`).

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain to configure (positional); the default keychain when omitted.

symbols.name: SecuritySetKeyPartitionListSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `security set-key-partition-list`, which lets Apple's signing
tools use a key without the "allow access" prompt that hangs a headless
build.

members.name: partition_list
members.doc:
Partition ids to allow (`-S`, comma-joined); repeatable. `apple-tool:`
and `apple:` cover `codesign` and the other Apple tools.

members.name: private_keys
members.doc: Match private keys only (`-s`).

members.name: password
members.doc:
The keychain's password (`-k`). A secret: masked in every rendering of
the command. Without it `security` prompts for one.

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain to modify (positional); the default keychain when omitted.

symbols.name: SecuritySettings
symbols.doc:
The shared settings of every `security` subcommand: the binary, and the
secret handling for the passwords a subcommand takes. A subclass names its
subcommand and builds its own arguments.

members.name: create_keychain
members.signature: static async create_keychain(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecurityCreateKeychainSettings], SecurityCreateKeychainSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Create a keychain with `security create-keychain`.

members.name: delete_keychain
members.signature: static async delete_keychain(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecurityDeleteKeychainSettings], SecurityDeleteKeychainSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Delete a keychain with `security delete-keychain`.

members.name: unlock_keychain
members.signature: static async unlock_keychain(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecurityUnlockKeychainSettings], SecurityUnlockKeychainSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Unlock a keychain with `security unlock-keychain`.

members.name: set_keychain_settings
members.signature: static async set_keychain_settings(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecuritySetKeychainSettings], SecuritySetKeychainSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Change a keychain's lock settings with `security set-keychain-settings`.

members.name: import_
members.signature: static async import_(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecurityImportSettings], SecurityImportSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Import a certificate or key with `security import`.

members.name: set_key_partition_list
members.signature: static async set_key_partition_list(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecuritySetKeyPartitionListSettings], SecuritySetKeyPartitionListSettings]) -> ExecResult
members.doc: Set which tools may use a key with `security set-key-partition-list`.

members.name: list_keychains
members.signature: static async list_keychains(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecurityListKeychainsSettings], SecurityListKeychainsSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Read — or, with `.set(...)`, replace — the keychain search list with
`security list-keychains`. Returns the listed paths; empty after a set,
which prints nothing.

members.name: find_identity
members.signature: static async find_identity(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[SecurityFindIdentitySettings], SecurityFindIdentitySettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc: List signing identities with `security find-identity`, parsed.

members.name: password
members.doc:
The keychain's password (`-p`). A secret: masked in every rendering of
the command. Without it `security` prompts for one.

members.name: keychain
members.doc: The keychain to unlock (positional); the default keychain when omitted.

members.name: certificate
members.doc:
The signing certificate and its private key, as a base64-encoded `.p12`
— the form CI secrets hold it in. Whitespace is ignored. Required. It is
decoded only into a `0600` file that is deleted straight after import,
and never appears in a command line or an error message.

members.name: certificate_password
members.doc:
The `.p12`'s export password, handed to `security import -P`. A secret:
masked in every rendering of that command. Defaults to empty, for a
`.p12` exported without one — `security` would otherwise prompt.

members.name: identity
members.doc:
Pick the identity whose name contains `filter`, or whose SHA-1 hash it
is. Needed only when the `.p12` holds more than one codesigning identity.

members.name: application
members.doc:
An application allowed to use the imported key (`security import -T`);
repeatable. Defaults to `/usr/bin/codesign` when none is named.

members.name: tool_path
members.doc: Run this `security` binary instead of the one on `PATH`.

members.name: bundle_id
members.doc: The app's bundle id, e.g. `com.example.app`; required.

members.name: build_number
members.doc: The uploaded build's number, `CFBundleVersion`; required.

members.name: version
members.doc:
The uploaded build's version, `CFBundleShortVersionString` — needed when
the same build number exists under several versions.

members.name: platform
members.doc: The build's platform — needed when the app ships on several.

members.name: timeout
members.doc: The longest wait for the build to finish processing (`"45m"`, or ms); default 30 minutes.

members.name: poll_interval
members.doc: The time between two looks at the build (`"1m"`, or ms); default 30 seconds.

members.name: uses_non_exempt_encryption
members.doc:
Answer the export-compliance question: whether the app uses encryption
beyond the exempt kinds. Until it is answered — here, or by
`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` in `Info.plist` — the build sits at
*Missing Compliance* and no tester can install it.

members.name: what_to_test

members.doc: The "What to Test" notes testers see, per locale; default locale `en-US`.

members.name: group

members.doc: Submit the build for beta review, which external testing needs.

Wait for an uploaded build to be processed, then distribute it in

The project flags every build action takes. Each action names itself and

symbols.doc: Settings for `AwsTasks.metricValue`: a `get-metric-data` request, and how to read it.

members.doc:
The series to read, by query id. Needed only when the request returns
more than one — hide the inputs of an expression with
`.returnData(false)` and it is not.

members.doc:
How to turn the series into one number (default `"latest"`, the newest
datapoint). An aggregate combines the datapoints the window holds: a

Return `value` when the series has no datapoints, instead of failing.

of errors, no data does mean `0`; for a latency or a CPU reading it
usually means the query is looking in the wrong place.

the command always runs quietly — the URL is captured, never streamed — and
the URL and that token are registered with the run's redactor.

symbols.name: AwsSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for an `aws` invocation.

Every instance sets two variables in the child's environment so the CLI
can never sit waiting for a keypress in a build: `AWS_PAGER` to the empty
string (CLI v2 pipes output through `less` by default) and
`AWS_CLI_AUTO_PROMPT` to `off` (a profile's `cli_auto_prompt` would
otherwise open the interactive prompt). Setting them there keeps the argv
exactly what the settings say; override either with `.env({...})`, or add
the explicit flag with noCliPager.

members.name: profile
members.doc: The named profile from the shared config and credentials files (`--profile`).

members.name: region
members.doc: The AWS Region to send the request to (`--region`), e.g. `"eu-west-1"`.

members.name: output
members.doc: The output format (`--output`): `json`, `text`, `table`, `yaml` or `yaml-stream`.

members.name: query
members.doc: A JMESPath expression that filters the response (`--query`).

members.name: endpoint_url
members.doc: Send the request to this URL instead of the service's default endpoint (`--endpoint-url`).

members.name: no_cli_pager
members.doc:
Pass `--no-cli-pager` explicitly. The pager is already off through
`AWS_PAGER` (see AwsSettings); the flag is for a build that wants
it on the command line as well. AWS CLI v2 only.

members.name: no_verify_ssl
members.doc:
Skip TLS certificate verification (`--no-verify-ssl`). This disables the
check that the endpoint is who it claims to be — meant for a local
emulator, never for a real account; prefer caBundle.

members.name: no_sign_request
members.doc: Send the request unsigned, without loading credentials (`--no-sign-request`).

members.name: ca_bundle
members.doc: The CA certificate bundle to verify TLS against (`--ca-bundle`).

members.name: cli_read_timeout
members.doc: The socket read timeout in seconds; `0` blocks forever (`--cli-read-timeout`).

members.name: cli_connect_timeout
members.doc: The socket connect timeout in seconds; `0` blocks forever (`--cli-connect-timeout`).

members.name: debug
members.doc:
Turn on the CLI's debug logging (`--debug`), written to stderr.

**The debug log carries credentials**: request headers with the session
token, and response bodies — a secret's value among them. The access key,
secret key and session token in the environment are registered with the
run's redactor when this is called, but a credential the CLI loads from a
profile, an SSO cache or a role is not known here and is not masked. Keep
it for a local investigation, never a shared CI log.

members.name: flag
members.signature: flag(name: str, value: str | float | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Add an arbitrary option: `--name value`, or the bare `--name`.

Two hazards come with the escape hatch, which the typed setters guard and
this does not: a value that starts with `-` is read by the CLI as the next
option, and a value that starts with `file://` or `fileb://` is replaced
by that file's contents — which then leave the machine in the request.
Never pass an untrusted value here.

symbols.doc:
Settings for `aws ssm get-parameter`.

A parameter may be a `SecureString`, so the command always runs quietly —

returns is registered with the run's redactor.

members.name: name
members.doc: The parameter's name or ARN (`--name`).

members.name: with_decryption
members.doc:
Return a `SecureString` decrypted (`--with-decryption`). Without it, a
`SecureString` comes back as ciphertext.

symbols.name: AwsSsmPutParameterSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `aws ssm put-parameter`.

`--value` is a command-line argument, which every user on the host can read
from the process table. For a `SecureString`, write the value to a file
with owner-only permissions and use valueFile: the CLI reads it, so
it never appears in the argv. A literal value given to a
`SecureString` is registered with the run's redactor, which masks Zuke's
own output but not the process table.

members.name: name
members.doc: The parameter's name (`--name`).

members.name: value
members.doc:
The value, given literally (`--value`). Refuses a value starting with
`file://` or `fileb://`: the CLI would read the named file rather than
store the text — use valueFile when that is the intent.

members.name: value_file
members.doc:
Read the value from a file (`--value=file://<path>`), which keeps it off
the command line. The CLI stores the file's contents exactly, trailing
newline included.

members.name: type_
members.doc: The parameter's type (`--type`).

members.name: overwrite
members.doc: Replace an existing parameter (`--overwrite`).

members.name: key_id
members.doc: The KMS key that encrypts a `SecureString` (`--key-id`).

members.name: description
members.doc: A description of the parameter (`--description`).

members.name: tier
members.doc: The storage tier (`--tier`).

members.name: data_type
members.doc: The data type (`--data-type`), e.g. `"aws:ec2:image"`.

The response carries a secret access key and a session token, so the

packages.summary: `@zuke/az` 1.2.1: `@zuke/az` — typed Azure CLI tasks, readers, and a canary platform and analysis.

symbols.name: AzAccountGetAccessTokenSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az account get-access-token`.

The answer is a bearer token, so the command always runs quietly —
captured, never streamed — with `--output json` pinned whatever the
settings or the user's config say, and the token is registered with the
run's redactor once it returns.

members.name: resource
members.doc: The resource the token is for, as a Microsoft Entra v1.0 endpoint (`--resource`).

members.name: resource_type
members.doc: A well-known resource the token is for (`--resource-type`).

members.name: scope
members.doc: Microsoft Entra v2.0 scopes for the token (`--scope`); repeatable.

members.name: tenant
members.doc: The tenant to get the token from (`--tenant`).

members.name: all
members.doc: Include subscriptions from every cloud and in every state (`--all`).

members.name: refresh
members.doc: Read the subscriptions from the server, not the cache (`--refresh`).

symbols.name: AzAccountSetSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az account set`: make a subscription the default. Name it
with the global `.subscription(nameOrId)`, which `account set` requires.

symbols.name: AzAccountShowSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `az account show`: the current (or the given) subscription.

symbols.name: AzAcrBuildSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az acr build`: build an image in the registry from a local
directory, a git URL or a tarball, and push it.

`--build-arg` values are visible to the ACR team for debugging, as the CLI
warns; pass a credential with secretBuildArg, whose value is also
registered with the run's redactor.

members.name: registry
members.doc: The registry to build in (`--registry`).

members.name: source
members.doc: The build context: a directory, a git URL or a tarball URL (the positional source).

members.name: image
members.doc: A `name:tag` to give the image (`--image`); repeatable.

members.name: file
members.doc: The Dockerfile, relative to the source (`--file`).

members.name: build_arg
members.doc: A build argument (`--build-arg name=value`); repeatable. Never a credential.

members.name: secret_build_arg
members.doc:
A build argument the ACR team does not see (`--secret-build-arg
name=value`); repeatable. The value is registered with the run's
redactor; it is still part of the argv.

members.name: platform
members.doc: The platform to build for (`--platform`), e.g. `"linux/arm64"`.

members.name: target
members.doc: The Dockerfile stage to build (`--target`).

members.name: timeout
members.doc: The build's timeout in seconds (`--timeout`).

members.name: resource_group
members.doc: The registry's resource group (`--resource-group`).

members.name: no_push
members.doc: Build without pushing (`--no-push`).

members.name: no_logs
members.doc: Do not stream the build's logs (`--no-logs`).

members.name: no_wait
members.doc: Return once the build is queued (`--no-wait`).

symbols.name: AzAcrLoginSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az acr login`.

Without exposeToken the CLI logs the local Docker client in itself.
With it, the CLI prints a registry refresh token instead — for
`docker login` with the user `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` — so the
command always runs quietly with `--output json` pinned, and the token is
registered with the run's redactor once it returns.

members.name: name
members.doc: The registry's name (`--name`).

members.name: expose_token
members.doc: Print a token instead of logging Docker in (`--expose-token`).

members.name: username
members.doc: A registry user, instead of the signed-in identity (`--username`).

members.name: password
members.doc:
The registry user's password (`--password`), sent on standard input as
`--password=@-` so it never enters the argv, and registered with the
run's redactor.

members.name: suffix
members.doc: The tenant suffix of the registry's login server (`--suffix`).

symbols.name: AzAcrRepositoryDeleteSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az acr repository delete`: one image, by tag or digest, or a
whole repository. The CLI asks for confirmation unless yes is set.

members.name: name
members.doc: The registry's name (`--name`).

members.name: image
members.doc: The image to delete, `repo:tag` or `repo@digest` (`--image`).

members.name: repository
members.doc: Delete the whole repository, every tag in it (`--repository`).

members.name: yes
members.doc: Delete without asking (`--yes`).

members.name: name
members.doc: The registry's name (`--name`).

members.name: repository
members.doc: The repository whose tags to list (`--repository`).

members.name: top
members.doc: At most this many tags (`--top`).

members.name: orderby
members.doc: Order by time, oldest or newest first (`--orderby`); by name otherwise.

members.name: detail
members.doc: Each tag's details, not only its name (`--detail`).

symbols.name: AzAksGetCredentialsSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az aks get-credentials`. The credentials go to a file —
`~/.kube/config` unless file says otherwise. Printing them
(`--file -`) would put a cluster credential in the build log, so a `-` is
refused.

members.name: admin
members.doc: Get the cluster-admin credentials (`--admin`).

members.name: file
members.doc: The kubeconfig file to write (`--file`); `~/.kube/config` by default.

members.name: overwrite_existing
members.doc: Replace an existing entry of the same name (`--overwrite-existing`).

members.name: context
members.doc: The context name to write, instead of the cluster's (`--context`).

members.name: public_fqdn
members.doc: Point the kubeconfig at the cluster's public FQDN (`--public-fqdn`).

members.name: format
members.doc: The credential format (`--format`): `azure` or `exec` (kubelogin).

symbols.name: AzContainerappIngressTrafficSetSettings

members.name: revision_weight
members.doc:
A revision's share of traffic, in percent (`--revision-weight
revision=weight`); repeatable. `"latest"` is the newest revision.

members.name: label_weight
members.doc: A label's share of traffic, in percent (`--label-weight label=weight`); repeatable.

members.name: all
members.doc: Include inactive revisions (`--all`).

symbols.name: AzContainerappRevisionSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az containerapp revision activate` and `deactivate`: the
app, and the revision to switch.

members.name: revision
members.doc: The revision to activate or deactivate (`--revision`).

symbols.name: AzContainerappShowSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `az containerapp show`. Secrets stay out: `--show-secrets` is not typed.

symbols.name: AzContainerappUpdateSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az containerapp update`: a new image, environment or scale,
which makes a new revision.

members.name: image
members.doc: The container image (`--image`), e.g. `"myregistry.azurecr.io/api:1.4.0"`.

members.name: container_name
members.doc: The container to update, when the app has several (`--container-name`).

members.name: revision_suffix
members.doc: A suffix for the new revision's name (`--revision-suffix`).

members.name: set_env_var
remove_env_vars
members.doc: Remove environment variables (`--remove-env-vars`); repeatable.

members.name: cpu
members.doc: CPU cores for the container (`--cpu`), e.g. `0.5`.

members.name: memory
members.doc: Memory for the container (`--memory`), e.g. `"1.0Gi"`.

members.name: min_replicas
members.doc: The fewest replicas (`--min-replicas`).

members.name: max_replicas
members.doc: The most replicas (`--max-replicas`).

members.name: yaml
members.doc: Take the whole configuration from a YAML file (`--yaml`); other options are ignored.

members.name: no_wait
members.doc: Return once the deployment has started (`--no-wait`).

symbols.name: AzDeploymentGroupTemplateSettings
symbols.doc:
The template, parameters and mode a deploying `deployment group` command
shares — `create` and `what-if` read them identically. The deployment's
`--name` is optional here; the CLI defaults it to the template file's name.

members.name: template_file
members.doc: A local ARM template or Bicep file (`--template-file`).

members.name: template_uri
members.doc: A template at a URL (`--template-uri`).

members.name: template_spec
members.doc: A template spec, by resource id (`--template-spec`).

members.name: parameters_file
members.doc:
A parameters file — JSON or `.bicepparam` (`--parameters <path>`);
repeatable, later values winning.

members.name: parameter
members.signature: parameter(name: str, value: str | float | bool) -> Self
members.doc:
One parameter (`--parameters name=value`); repeatable. The value is
converted to the type the template declares. It is part of the argv, so a
secure value belongs in a parameters file or a Key Vault reference.

members.name: mode
members.doc: `Incremental` (the default) or `Complete`, which deletes what the template omits (`--mode`).

symbols.name: AzDeploymentGroupWhatIfSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `az deployment group what-if`: what a deployment would change.

members.name: result_format
members.doc: How much of each change to show (`--result-format`).

members.name: exclude_change_types
members.doc: Leave these kinds of change out (`--exclude-change-types`); repeatable.

members.name: no_pretty_print
members.doc: Print the result as JSON rather than the formatted diff (`--no-pretty-print`).

symbols.name: AzFunctionappDeploymentSourceConfigZipSettings

members.name: src
members.doc: The zip package (`--src`).

members.name: build_remote
members.doc: Build the package on the service — install dependencies there (`--build-remote`).

members.name: timeout
members.doc: How long to wait for the deployment's status, in seconds (`--timeout`).

members.name: slot
members.doc: A slot instead of production (`--slot`).

members.name: name
members.doc: The resource group's name (`--name`).

members.name: location
members.doc: The region to create it in (`--location`), e.g. `"westeurope"`.

members.name: tag
members.doc: A tag (`--tags key=value`); repeatable.

members.name: managed_by
members.doc: The id of the resource that manages the group (`--managed-by`).

symbols.name: AzGroupDeleteSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az group delete`. The CLI asks for confirmation unless
yes is set — and fails, without a terminal to ask on.

members.name: name
members.doc: The resource group's name (`--name`).

members.name: yes
members.doc: Delete without asking (`--yes`).

members.name: no_wait
members.doc: Return once the deletion has started (`--no-wait`).

members.name: force_deletion_types
members.doc: Force-delete the group's resources of this type (`--force-deletion-types`).

symbols.name: AzGroupExistsSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for `az group exists`, which prints `true` or `false`.

members.name: name
members.doc: The resource group's name (`--name`).

members.name: name
members.doc: The resource group's name (`--name`).

symbols.name: AzKeyvaultSecretSetSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az keyvault secret set`.

The value comes from a file — read exactly, with its
encoding — or from value, which is sent on standard input
as `--value=@-` so it never enters the argv. The CLI strips trailing line
breaks from what it reads that way; use a file for a value that must keep
them.

members.name: vault_name
members.doc: The vault's name (`--vault-name`).

members.name: name
members.doc: The secret's name (`--name`).

members.name: value
members.doc:
The value, sent on standard input as `--value=@-` and registered with the
run's redactor.

members.name: file
members.doc: Read the value from a file (`--file`) — the way to keep it exact.

members.name: encoding
members.doc:
How the file is encoded (`--encoding`); `utf-8` by default.
Refused without a file: the CLI saves it as a `file-encoding` tag that
`keyvault secret download` later decodes with.

members.name: content_type
members.doc: What the value is, e.g. `"password"` (`--content-type`).

members.name: expires
members.doc:
When the secret expires (`--expires`): a `Date`, or a string such as
`2027-01-01T00:00:00Z` — the CLI takes UTC to the second, no fractions.

members.name: not_before
members.doc: When the secret becomes usable (`--not-before`), in the same form as expires.

members.name: disabled
members.doc: Create the secret disabled, or enabled (`--disabled`).

members.name: tag
members.doc: A tag (`--tags key=value`); repeatable.

members.name: vault_name
members.doc: The vault's name (`--vault-name`).

members.name: name
members.doc: The secret's name (`--name`).

members.name: version
members.doc: A specific version; the latest when omitted (`--version`).

members.name: id
members.doc: The secret's full identifier, instead of vault and name (`--id`).

symbols.name: AzLoginSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az login`, for the non-interactive forms a build uses. The
interactive browser and device-code forms are left to `.command("login")`.

Exactly one credential is sent: a secret (password), a
certificate or a federatedToken for a service principal,
or identity for a managed identity. A service principal without
one would make the CLI prompt for a password, so it is refused here.

`az login` reads the global `.subscription(...)` as the subscription to
make the default once it has signed in. Its output lists the account's
subscriptions — no credential — so it is not masked.

members.name: service_principal
members.doc: Log in as a service principal (`--service-principal`).

members.name: username
members.doc: The service principal's client id (`--username`).

members.name: tenant
members.doc: The Microsoft Entra tenant, required for a service principal (`--tenant`).

members.name: password
members.doc:
The service principal's client secret (`--password`), sent on standard
input as `--password=@-` so it never enters the argv, and registered with
the run's redactor. Prefer federatedToken (no long-lived secret)
or certificate.

members.name: federated_token
members.doc:
A federated token (OIDC) to exchange for the service principal's access
(`--federated-token`), sent on standard input as `--federated-token=@-`
and registered with the run's redactor.

members.name: certificate
members.doc: A PEM file with the service principal's key and certificate (`--certificate`).

members.name: use_cert_sn_issuer
members.doc:
Authenticate with Subject Name + Issuer, for automatic certificate
rolls (`--use-cert-sn-issuer`).

members.name: identity
members.doc: Log in with the managed identity of the machine the build runs on (`--identity`).

members.name: client_id
members.doc: A user-assigned managed identity, by client id (`--client-id`).

members.name: object_id
members.doc: A user-assigned managed identity, by object id (`--object-id`).

members.name: resource_id
members.doc: A user-assigned managed identity, by resource id (`--resource-id`).

members.name: allow_no_subscriptions
members.doc: Succeed for a tenant with no subscriptions (`--allow-no-subscriptions`).

members.name: username
members.doc: The account to log out; the active one when omitted (`--username`).

symbols.name: AzMonitorActivityLogListSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az monitor activity-log list`: the control-plane events of a
subscription, resource group or resource. The CLI returns at most
maxEvents — 50 unless told otherwise.

members.name: start_time
members.doc: The start of the range (`--start-time`).

members.name: end_time
members.doc: The end of the range (`--end-time`); now by default.

members.name: offset
members.doc: The length of the range when only one end is given (`--offset`); six hours by default.

members.name: resource_group
members.doc: Only events in this resource group (`--resource-group`).

members.name: resource_id
members.doc: Only events on this resource (`--resource-id`).

members.name: namespace
members.doc: Only events from this resource provider (`--namespace`).

members.name: caller
members.doc: Only events by this caller (`--caller`).

members.name: status
members.doc: Only events with this status, e.g. `"Failed"` (`--status`).

members.name: correlation_id
members.doc: Only the events of this operation (`--correlation-id`).

members.name: max_events
members.doc: The most events to return (`--max-events`); 50 by default.

members.name: select
members.doc: Only these properties of each event (`--select`); repeatable.

members.name: workspace
members.doc: The workspace's id — its customer id, a GUID (`--workspace`).

members.name: analytics_query
members.doc: The KQL query (`--analytics-query`).

symbols.name: AzMonitorMetricsListSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az monitor metrics list`: a resource's metrics over a time
range, one datapoint per interval.

The CLI returns at most top time series per metric — ten unless
told otherwise — so a query that splits by a dimension can silently lose
series; raise `top` to cover them.

members.name: resource
members.doc: The resource, by full resource id (`--resource`).

members.name: metrics
members.doc: The metrics to read, by name (`--metrics`); repeatable.

members.name: aggregation
members.doc: The aggregations to compute per interval (`--aggregation`); repeatable.

members.name: interval
members.doc:
The time grain of each datapoint (`--interval`); one minute by default.
The range set by window is not aligned to it, so the newest
datapoint may cover an interval that is still being written.

members.name: start_time
members.doc: The start of the range (`--start-time`).

members.name: end_time
members.doc: The end of the range (`--end-time`); now by default.

members.name: window
members.signature: window(duration: str | float, end: str | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
The `duration` (`"15m"`, or milliseconds) up to `end` — now, unless
given — as `--start-time` and `--end-time`.

members.name: offset
members.doc:
The length of the range when only one end is given (`--offset`, as
`"30m"` or milliseconds); an hour by default.

members.name: filter
members.doc:
An OData filter on the dimensions (`--filter`), e.g.
`"ApiName eq 'GetBlob' and GeoType eq '*'"`. For plain equality, prefer
dimension, which quotes the value.

members.name: dimension
members.doc:
Only the series where the dimension `name` is `value` — rendered into
`--filter` as `name eq 'value'`, joined with `and`; repeatable.

members.name: split_by
members.doc: Split the series by these dimensions (`--dimension`); repeatable.

members.name: namespace
members.doc: The metric namespace (`--namespace`).

members.name: top
members.doc: The most time series to return per metric (`--top`); 10 by default.

members.name: orderby
members.doc: The aggregation and direction to sort series by (`--orderby`), e.g. `"sum desc"`.

symbols.name: AzMonitorMetricValueSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `AzTasks.metricValue`: a `metrics list` request with exactly
one AzMonitorMetricsListSettings.aggregation, and how to read it.

members.name: metric
members.doc:
The metric to read, by name. Needed only when the request names more
than one with `.metrics(...)`.

members.name: aggregate
members.doc:
How to turn the datapoints into one number, across every series the
answer holds. `"latest"` (the default) is the newest interval — the sum
of the series' values at the newest timestamp any of them has, so a
metric split by a dimension reads as its total. The others combine every
datapoint in the range: a `"sum"` of per-minute `Total`s is the range's
total.

members.name: missing_data_as
members.doc:
Return `value` when there are no datapoints, instead of failing. Azure
Monitor reports an interval with no events without a value, so for a
count of errors no data does mean `0`; for a latency it usually means the
query is looking in the wrong place.

symbols.name: AzSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for an `az` invocation.

Every instance sets three of the CLI's configuration variables in the
child's environment, so the CLI never waits on a keypress, installs code,
or colours a build log:

- `AZURE_EXTENSION_USE_DYNAMIC_INSTALL=no` — a command from an extension
  that is not installed fails, instead of prompting (on a terminal) or
  silently downloading and installing the extension (without one). The
  CLI's message does not name the extension — it says the command `is
  misspelled or not recognized by the system` and exits 2 — so install what
  a build needs up front with `az extension add --name <name>`.
- `AZURE_CORE_LOGIN_EXPERIENCE_V2=off` — an interactive `az login` does not
  open its subscription selector.
- `AZURE_CORE_NO_COLOR=true` — no ANSI colour codes in captured output.

Setting them there keeps the argv exactly what the settings say; override
any of them with `.env({...})`. A confirmation prompt (`group delete`
without `--yes`) is not switched off: on a terminal it asks, without one
the CLI fails — call the command's `.yes()` to confirm in the build.

members.name: subscription
members.doc:
The subscription to run against, by name or id (`--subscription`); the
CLI's default subscription when omitted. Most commands take it; the
`account` commands read it as the subscription they act on.

members.name: output
members.doc:
The output format (`--output`): `json`, `jsonc`, `yaml`, `yamlc`,
`table`, `tsv` or `none`.

members.name: query
members.doc: A JMESPath expression that filters the output (`--query`).

members.name: only_show_errors
members.doc:
Print errors only, suppressing warnings (`--only-show-errors`). The CLI
refuses it beside `--debug` or `--verbose`, and so do these settings.

members.name: verbose
members.doc: More logging, on stderr (`--verbose`).

members.name: env
members.doc:
Merge additional environment variables for the process. Under
debug — set before or after — a credential variable set here is
registered with the run's redactor, like one in the build's environment.

members.name: debug
members.doc:
Turn on the CLI's debug logging (`--debug`), written to stderr.

**The debug log can carry credentials**: request and response details,
which for a Key Vault or storage command include what was read or sent.
The credentials the CLI reads from the environment — `AZURE_STORAGE_KEY`,
`AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `AZURE_STORAGE_SAS_TOKEN`,
`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT`, and Terraform's
`ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` beside them — are registered with the run's redactor,
whether they are in the build's environment or set with env, but a token the CLI holds in its own cache
(`~/.azure`) is not known here and is not masked. Keep it for a local
investigation, never a shared CI log.

members.name: flag
members.signature: flag(name: str, value: str | float | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Add an arbitrary option: `--name value`, or the bare `--name`.

Two hazards come with the escape hatch, which the typed setters guard and
this does not: a value that starts with `-` is read by the CLI as the next
option, and a value that starts with `@` — or, in a `key=value` list
element, a value after the `=` that does — is replaced by that file's
contents (`@-` by standard input), which then leave the machine in the
request. Never pass an untrusted value here, or through `.args(...)` or
`.command(...)`.

symbols.name: AzWebappConfigAppsettingsSetSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `az webapp config appsettings set`.

Each setting's value is part of the argv, so it is visible in the process
table and in the command line the build logs; a credential belongs in Key
Vault, referenced with keyVaultReference. A value that starts with
`@` is otherwise refused, because the CLI would read it from a file. The
CLI's answer lists every setting with its value redacted.

members.name: setting
members.doc: An app setting (`--settings name=value`); repeatable.

members.name: key_vault_reference
members.doc:
An app setting whose value App Service reads from Key Vault; repeatable.
Sent as the JSON object `{"name":"@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=<uri>)"}`,
a form `--settings` accepts: written as `name=@Microsoft…` the CLI would
first try to read a file of that name, and send its contents if one
existed.

A setting that stays with its slot through a swap (`--slot-settings
name=value`); repeatable.

members.name: slot
members.doc: A slot instead of production (`--slot`).

symbols.name: ChocoApikeySettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `choco apikey`, which manages the API keys choco saves per
source — so a later `choco push` to that source needs no key on its
command line.

``ts
await ChocoTasks.apikey((s) =>
  s.add().source("https://push.chocolatey.org/").apiKey(key)
);
``

`add` needs a source and an apiKey; `remove` needs a
source. With no action set, choco lists the saved keys (by source; it never
prints a key itself).

symbols.name: ChocoCommandSettings
symbols.doc:
Base for a typed `choco` command: the command, then its operands, then its
own options, then the common switches — the order choco's own usage lines
print (`choco install <pkg> [<options/switches>]`). Anything added through
the inherited `.command(...)`/`.flag(...)` escape hatches follows.

Valued options render as one `--name=value` token, the spelling choco's
help prints, so a value that starts with `-` stays the option's value
rather than becoming a switch of its own.

Operands are refused when choco would read them as a switch: a package id
or file path never starts with `-`, and passing `--force` as a "package"
would change what the command does rather than fail.

members.doc: Answer yes to every prompt (`--yes`), which also accepts licenses.

members.name: force
members.doc:
Force the behaviour (`--force`) — reinstall an installed package, say.
Choco warns against it in normal operation.

members.name: limit_output
members.doc: Print only the essential information (`--limit-output`).

members.name: verbose
members.doc: Print verbose messages (`--verbose`).

members.doc: Package ids to install (required); repeatable.

members.doc:
Where to find the packages (`--source`): a feed URL, or a local directory
holding `.nupkg` files. Defaults to the configured feeds.

members.doc:

members.name: frozen
members.doc:
Error out if the lockfile is out of date (`--frozen`). See
DenoPermissionSettings.frozen for why the name mirrors the real
Deno flag rather than `PnpmSettings.frozenLockfile()`'s naming.

members.name: paths
members.doc: The entry points to cache (at least one is required).

members.name: paths

members.name: all
members.doc:
Type-check remote modules and npm packages too (`--all`), not just the
local code. Slower, and the only way to catch a dependency whose published
types do not actually compile.

members.doc: Type-check the code blocks in JSDoc and Markdown as well (`--doc`).

members.name: doc_only
members.doc: Type-check *only* the code blocks in JSDoc and Markdown (`--doc-only`).

members.doc: Type-check JavaScript files too (`--check-js`).

members.name: config
members.doc:
Type-check against a specific configuration file (`--config`) instead of the
one Deno would discover by walking up from the checked files.

The discovered config decides how bare specifiers resolve, so pointing at
another one type-checks the same sources against a different dependency
set — for example checking a workspace member against the *published*
version of a sibling it declares, rather than the local member that
workspace resolution would substitute.

members.name: no_config

members.name: no_lock
members.doc:
Ignore the lockfile entirely (`--no-lock`), neither reading nor writing it.

Use it for a check whose resolutions are deliberately not the project's:
writing them into the committed lock would corrupt it, and reading it would
pin the very versions the check is trying to vary.

members.name: frozen
members.doc:
Error out if the lockfile is out of date (`--frozen`). See
DenoPermissionSettings.frozen for why the name mirrors the real
Deno flag rather than `PnpmSettings.frozenLockfile()`'s naming.

members.name: lock
members.doc: Use an explicit lockfile (`--lock`) instead of the discovered `deno.lock`.

members.name: import_map
members.doc: Load an import map from a file or URL (`--import-map`).

members.name: skip_types
members.doc:
Exclude `@types/*` packages (`--skip-types`). Deno selects them by name,
so a package that ships runtime code under a `@types/` name is skipped
too.

members.doc: Cross-compile for another platform (`--target`).

members.name: include
members.doc:
Embed an extra module, file or directory (`--include`, repeatable).

Needed for anything the module graph cannot see statically — a
dynamically imported module, a worker entrypoint, or a data file the
program reads at runtime.

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Exclude a file or directory from what include embedded (`--exclude`).

members.name: exclude_unused_npm
members.doc:
Embed only the npm packages the module graph actually reaches
(`--exclude-unused-npm`), instead of the whole lockfile snapshot.

Packages reached only through a dynamic import are not statically
traceable, so pass those to include explicitly.

members.doc: Set the executable's Windows icon from a `.ico` file (`--icon`).

members.name: no_terminal
members.doc: Hide the console window on Windows (`--no-terminal`).

members.name: self_extracting
members.doc:
Produce a self-extracting binary (`--self-extracting`) that unpacks its
embedded file system to disk on first run and executes from there.

members.name: bundle
members.doc:
Bundle the entrypoint before embedding it (`--bundle`), rather than
shipping the whole `node_modules` tree. Experimental: it produces a
smaller, faster-starting binary but drops dynamic `require`/`import`
patterns that cannot be traced statically.

members.name: minify
members.doc:
Minify the bundled output (`--minify`). Requires bundle — the CLI
rejects `--minify` on its own, and so does this wrapper, so the mistake
surfaces while the argv is being built rather than after the compile
starts.

members.name: config
members.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

members.name: no_check
members.doc: Skip type-checking before compiling (`--no-check`).

members.name: dir
members.doc: The coverage profile directory to report on.

members.name: lcov
members.doc: Emit lcov instead of the table report (`--lcov`).

members.name: output
members.doc: Write the report to a file (`--output=`).

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Exclude files matching the pattern (`--exclude=`).

members.name: include
members.doc: Report only on files matching the pattern (`--include=`).

members.name: ignore
members.doc: Skip files matching these patterns (`--ignore=`).

members.name: html
members.doc:
Write an HTML report into the profile directory (`--html`).

Mutually exclusive with lcov and with any threshold: given both,
deno emits the lcov and silently produces no HTML, so asking for both is
refused rather than quietly honoured in half.

members.name: detailed
members.doc: Report per-line detail alongside the summary table (`--detailed`).

members.name: lines_threshold
members.doc:
Fail the gate if line coverage is below `percent`. `deno coverage` has no
fail-under flag, so DenoTasks.coverage enforces this after parsing
the lcov report (and forces `--lcov` so a report exists to parse).

members.name: branches_threshold
members.doc: Fail the gate if branch coverage is below `percent` (see linesThreshold).

members.name: threshold
members.doc: Fail the gate if either line or branch coverage is below `percent`.

members.name: per_file_threshold
members.doc:
Fail the gate if any single instrumented file's line coverage is below
`percent` — a per-file floor, so an under-tested file can't hide inside a
healthy aggregate (see CoverageThresholds.perFile, which notes the
`deno coverage` limit for files no test loads).

members.name: frozen
members.doc:

DenoPermissionSettings.frozen for why the name mirrors the real
Deno flag.

members.name: no_lock
members.doc: Ignore the lockfile entirely (`--no-lock`), neither reading nor writing it.

members.name: lock
members.doc: Use an explicit lockfile (`--lock`) instead of the discovered `deno.lock`.

members.name: filters
members.doc:
Restrict the report to dependencies matching these filters, which may
include `*` wildcards. Filters match the alias a dependency is declared
under, not the package it resolves to.

members.name: compatible
members.doc: Only consider versions satisfying the declared semver range (`--compatible`).

members.name: latest
members.doc: Consider the latest version regardless of the declared range (`--latest`).

members.name: recursive
members.doc: Include every workspace member (`--recursive`).

members.name: update
members.doc:
Write the newer versions back into the manifest (`--update`) instead of
only reporting them. Without it `deno outdated` reports and changes
nothing, which is what a freshness gate wants.

members.name: lockfile_only

members.name: allow_dirty

members.name: allow_slow_types
