symbols.name: DenoPermissionSettings
symbols.doc: Base for subcommands that accept `--allow-*` permission flags.

members.name: allow_all
members.doc: Grant all permissions (`--allow-all`).

members.name: allow
members.doc: Grant one permission, optionally scoped to values (`--allow-read=a,b`).

members.name: frozen
members.doc:
Error out if the lockfile is out of date instead of silently updating it
(`--frozen`). Use it whenever the module graph must match the committed
`deno.lock` exactly — running an `npm:` tool in CI, say, so its transitive
tree stays pinned to the audited integrity hashes rather than being
resolved afresh. Named `frozen` — not `frozenLockfile` — to mirror the real
Deno CLI flag exactly. This is a deliberate divergence from
`PnpmSettings.frozenLockfile()` in `@zuke/pnpm`, which follows pnpm's own
flag name instead: guideline 7 (mirror the real CLI) takes priority over
cross-package naming symmetry.

members.name: allow_dirty
members.doc: Publish even with an uncommitted working tree (`--allow-dirty`).

members.name: allow_slow_types
members.doc: Permit slow types in the published package (`--allow-slow-types`).

members.name: no_check
members.doc: Skip type-checking before publishing (`--no-check`).

members.name: dry_run
members.doc: Validate without publishing (`--dry-run`).

members.name: config
members.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

members.name: token
members.doc:
Authenticate with a token instead of interactive/OIDC auth (`--token`).

Registered with the run's redactor, so every *rendering* of the command
masks it — a dry-run echo, a failure message. That is as far as it goes:
`deno publish` accepts the token only as a flag, so the value still
reaches the child's argv, where `ps` and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` expose it to
every other user on the host and to every process the build starts.

There is no environment variable to move it to. `DENO_AUTH_TOKENS` is not
one — it authenticates *module fetches*, not publishing.

Prefer passing no token at all. On GitHub Actions `deno publish` uses OIDC,
so the publish is authenticated by the workflow's identity and there is no
credential to expose; this repository's own publish does exactly that.

members.name: set_version
members.doc:
Publish under an overridden version (`--set-version`) instead of the one
in the manifest — how a release job publishes a version it computed
without first committing it.

deno accepts it only when publishing a single package: it is rejected in
a workspace, where the versions have to come from each member's own
manifest. Whether the working directory is a workspace is not visible
while the argv is being built, so this is a note rather than a refusal.

members.name: no_provenance
members.doc:
Disable provenance attestation (`--no-provenance`).

Provenance is what lets a consumer verify the published artifact came from
this repository's CI, so turning it off is a deliberate weakening rather
than a default worth reaching for. It stays on unless this is called.

deno produces it by default only on GitHub Actions, so elsewhere there is
nothing to disable. The case it exists for is the trade it makes: the
attestation publicly links the package to the repository, workflow and
commit it was built from, which a package published from a private
repository may not want disclosed. Weigh that against consumers losing
the ability to verify the artifact's origin, and prefer keeping it.

members.name: password
members.doc:
The password (`-p`), which docker accepts and which therefore stays on the
wrapper.

Prefer passwordStdin. This flag puts the password in the child's
argv, and a child's argv is world-readable on a default Linux host —
through `ps` or `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` — to every other user on the machine
and every process the build starts. On a shared or self-hosted runner that
is every co-tenant.

The value is registered with the run's redactor, so Zuke's own renderings
of the command mask it. That does not cover the process table: the argv
handed to the operating system is not redacted, and docker itself warns
about `-p` for the same reason. Masking is what can be done here, not a
fix for the exposure.

members.name: password_stdin
members.doc:
Pipe the password to docker through STDIN (`--password-stdin`), which
keeps it off the command line entirely.

This is the route docker documents for exactly this reason, and the one to
use in CI. The token goes to the child's standard input, which — unlike its
argv — no other process on the host can read.

The password is required, because the flag on its own means nothing: it
tells docker to read standard input, and this wrapper is what has to put
something there. A `--password-stdin` with no writer leaves docker reading
a stream that is never written.

Without it compose starts or recreates a dependency that is stopped or

Classify `deno doc --lint` output across packages into real defects: every
`missing-jsdoc`, plus every `private-type-ref` whose referenced type is not
an accepted cross-package import (in the report's `crossPackageTypes`).

packages.name: zuke.tools.gcloud
packages.summary: `@zuke/gcloud` 1.4.2: `@zuke/gcloud` — typed Google Cloud tooling for Zuke builds: the `gcloud` (Google Cloud SDK) CLI wrapper, plus **GCS**, **Secret Manager** and **Cloud Monitoring** REST task groups that share `gcloud`-based auth (no Google SDK dependency), and canary support for Cloud Run rollouts gated on Cloud Monitoring.

symbols.name: CloudMonitoringMetricValueSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `CloudMonitoringTasks.metricValue`: a time-series read, and
how to turn it into one number. The view is always `FULL` — the reader
needs the points.

members.name: aggregate
members.doc:
How to turn the points into one number, across every series the answer
holds. `"latest"` (the default) sums each series' own newest point, so a
metric split by a label reads as its total. The others combine every
point in the window: a `"sum"` of per-minute `ALIGN_SUM` points is the
window's total.

A `DISTRIBUTION` point reads as its mean. `"average"` weights each mean
by its sample count; `"maximum"` and `"minimum"` are of the means.
Means cannot be added, so `"sum"` refuses distributions, and `"latest"`
refuses more than one distribution series — collapse them with
`.crossSeriesReducer(...)`, or align them to a number with
`ALIGN_PERCENTILE_99`, `ALIGN_MEAN` and the like.

members.name: missing_data_as
members.doc:
Return `value` when there are no points, instead of failing. Cloud
Monitoring writes no point for a period with no events, so for a count
of errors no data does mean `0`; for a latency it usually means the
filter is looking in the wrong place.

members.name: time_series_list
members.signature: static async time_series_list(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[CloudMonitoringTimeSeriesSettings], CloudMonitoringTimeSeriesSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Read the time series the settings describe, every page of them. A
series can arrive split across two pages; each part is returned as the
API sent it. Fails when the read still has a next page after
`.maxPages(n)` pages, rather than return part of the answer.

members.name: metric_value
members.signature: static async metric_value(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[CloudMonitoringMetricValueSettings], CloudMonitoringMetricValueSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
One number from the time series the settings describe: the latest
value, or an aggregate of every point in the window.

symbols.name: CloudMonitoringTimeSeriesSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for a Cloud Monitoring time-series read, configured through
`CloudMonitoringTasks.timeSeriesList((s) => …)`.

``ts
s.project("my-proj")
  .metricType("run.googleapis.com/request_count")
  .resourceType("cloud_run_revision")
  .resourceLabel("service_name", "api")
  .metricLabel("response_code_class", "5xx")
  .alignmentPeriod("60s").perSeriesAligner("ALIGN_SUM")
  .crossSeriesReducer("REDUCE_SUM")
  .window("15m")
``

members.name: project
members.doc:
The project to read from; when omitted, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (then
`GCLOUD_PROJECT`).

members.name: metric_type
members.doc:
The metric to read: `metric.type = "<type>"`, e.g.
`"run.googleapis.com/request_count"`. The API reads exactly one metric
type per call.

members.name: resource_type
members.doc: Only series on this monitored-resource type: `resource.type = "<type>"`.

members.name: resource_label
members.doc: Only series whose resource label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

members.name: metric_label
members.doc: Only series whose metric label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

members.name: filter
members.doc:
Raw text in the Monitoring filter language, joined with the typed parts
by `AND`; repeatable. It is the caller's own text and is not escaped —
never build it from an untrusted value. With no metricType, it
must name the metric itself.

members.name: window
members.doc:
How far back to read (`"15m"`, or ms; default five minutes), ending now
— or, with an alignmentPeriod, at the last period boundary, so
the period still being written is not read. The window must be at least
one period long.

members.name: interval
members.doc: Read exactly this interval instead of a window ending now.

members.name: alignment_period
members.doc:
What each aligned point covers (`aggregation.alignmentPeriod`) —
`"60s"`, `"5m"`, or ms; whole seconds, at least 60, as the API requires.

members.name: per_series_aligner
members.doc: How each series is aligned (`aggregation.perSeriesAligner`).

members.name: cross_series_reducer
members.doc: How aligned series are combined (`aggregation.crossSeriesReducer`).

members.name: group_by_fields
members.doc:
The labels the reducer keeps series apart by
(`aggregation.groupByFields`), e.g. `"resource.labels.revision_name"`.

members.name: view
members.doc: `FULL` (the default) returns points; `HEADERS` only each series' labels.

members.name: page_size
members.doc: The most results per page (`pageSize`; the API's default is 100,000).

members.name: max_pages
members.doc:
The most pages to read (default 100). A read that still has a next page
after that many fails — a partial answer is never returned as a whole.

members.name: delay
members.doc:
End the window this long before now (`"2m"`, or ms) — for the time a
metric takes to become readable. Google's metrics list gives it per
metric: Cloud Run's `request_count` and `request_latencies` are "not
visible for up to 120 seconds" after sampling. Without it the newest
points may not exist yet, or hold only part of their period. Default
`0` for a read; the `cloudMonitoring(...)` analysis defaults to two
minutes.

members.doc: A pre-resolved OAuth access token.

members.name: gcloud

Global gcloud flags for the default token read,

`.runner(...)`, the seam a test answers through. Unused when a
token or tokenProvider is set.

symbols.name: GcloudLoggingReadSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `gcloud logging read`: which entries (the filter), from where
(project, folder, organization, billing account, or a log view), and how
many.

members.name: filter
members.doc:
Raw filter text in the Logging query language, joined with every other
part by `AND`; repeatable. It is the caller's own text and is not
escaped — never build it from an untrusted value; use the typed setters
for those.

members.name: resource_type
members.doc: Only entries from this monitored-resource type: `resource.type="…"`.

members.name: resource_label
members.doc: Only entries whose resource label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

members.name: label
members.doc: Only entries whose own label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

members.name: min_severity
members.doc: Only entries at `severity` or above: `severity>=ERROR`.

members.name: since
members.doc: Only entries at or after `time`: `timestamp>="…"`.

members.name: until
members.doc: Only entries before `time`: `timestamp<"…"`.

members.name: freshness
members.doc:
Only entries newer than this — `"1h"`, `"90s"`, or ms — sent as an
explicit `timestamp>="<now − duration>"` in the filter, measured from
now. gcloud's own `--freshness` is not used: gcloud silently
drops it whenever the filter's text contains the word `timestamp`
anywhere, or the order is `asc`, and the read then spans the whole
retention period.

members.name: order
members.doc: Newest first (`desc`, gcloud's default) or oldest first (`--order`).

members.name: limit
members.doc: Read at most this many entries (`--limit`; gcloud's default is unlimited).

members.name: organization
members.doc:
Read from an organization's logs (`--organization`). gcloud takes one of
`--organization`, `--folder`, `--billing-account` and `--project`.

members.name: folder
members.doc: Read from a folder's logs (`--folder`).

members.name: billing_account
members.doc: Read from a billing account's logs (`--billing-account`).

members.name: log_view
members.signature: log_view(bucket: str, location: str, view: str) -> Self
members.doc: Read through a log view (`--bucket`, `--location`, `--view`).

members.name: resource_names
members.doc:
Read from these resources instead (`--resource-names`): a project,
folder or organization name, or a full log-view path. gcloud takes these
or a log view, not both.

symbols.name: GcloudRunServicesUpdateSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `gcloud run services update` — amending a service that already
exists.

Distinct from GcloudRunDeploySettings on purpose. `run deploy`
creates the service when it is absent and resets settings the invocation does
not name; `run services update` only ever amends an existing one. A deploy
that points a live service at a freshly built image wants the second
guarantee, and getting the first by accident — a service quietly created, or
scaling config quietly dropped — is a worse failure than an error.

members.name: service
members.doc: The service to update (positional).

members.name: region
members.doc: The region it runs in (`--region`).

members.name: platform
members.doc: The platform it runs on (`--platform`).

members.name: image
members.doc: The container image to point the service at (`--image`).

members.name: update_env_vars
members.doc:
Set or overwrite environment variables (`--update-env-vars`), as
`KEY=value`; repeatable. Variables the call does not name are left alone —
which is the difference from `run deploy`'s `--set-env-vars`.

members.name: remove_env_vars
members.doc: Remove environment variables by name (`--remove-env-vars`); repeatable.

members.name: clear_env_vars
members.doc: Remove every environment variable the service has (`--clear-env-vars`).

members.name: update_secrets
members.doc:
Set or overwrite Secret Manager mounts (`--update-secrets`), as
`KEY=secret:version`; repeatable.

members.name: memory
members.doc: Memory per instance (`--memory`), e.g. `"512Mi"`.

members.name: cpu
members.doc: CPU per instance (`--cpu`).

members.name: concurrency
members.doc: Requests served concurrently per instance (`--concurrency`).

members.name: max_instances
members.doc: Upper bound on instances (`--max-instances`).

members.name: min_instances
members.doc: Lower bound on instances (`--min-instances`).

members.doc: Tag the revision this update creates (`--tag`).

members.doc: Create the revision without moving traffic to it (`--no-traffic`).

members.name: to_tags

members.name: container_images_add_tag
members.doc:
Add tags to a container image across registries:
`gcloud container images add-tag <source> <destination…>`. Each argument is
a discrete argv token, so an image reference can't inject flags. Runs with
`--quiet` (the re-tag is non-interactive automation; `add-tag` otherwise
prompts for confirmation).

symbols.doc:

members.name: method

members.name: app_id
members.doc: The GitHub App's id (the `App ID` on its settings page).

members.name: private_key
members.doc:
The app's private key, as the PEM's **contents** — GitHub issues PKCS#1
(`BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`); PKCS#8 is accepted too.

members.name: owner
members.doc: The user or organisation the app is installed on.

members.name: repositories
members.doc:
Scope the token to these repositories (names only, without the owner).
Omit to cover every repository the installation can reach — prefer naming
them, so a leaked token is narrow.

members.name: permission
members.doc:
Request one permission, e.g. `.permission("contents", "write")`. Repeatable.
Narrowing to what the target needs beats inheriting the app's full set;
requesting more than the installation grants is an error from GitHub.

The API names multi-word permissions with underscores (`pull_requests`), so
a hyphen is normalised to one. That spelling is the trap here:
`create-github-app-token` takes its inputs as `permission-pull-requests`,
and passing that form straight through is rejected as a permission the
installation does not grant — which reads as a misconfigured app rather
than a misspelled key.

members.name: base_url
members.doc: Use a different REST base (GitHub Enterprise Server).

members.name: app
members.doc:
The App's credentials — its numeric id and the PEM contents of its
private key, as the build's parameters (`.secret()` for the key). Either
one unset at call time means "no App": the source yields the
fallback. Both are read when the token is first needed, never at
construction, so parameters declared on the build resolve first.

members.name: repository
members.doc:
The repository to mint for, as `owner/name`. Defaults to the repository
the run is on, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. Name it to refuse minting anywhere
else: a run whose `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is another repository then gets the
fallback, with a warning, rather than a token for this one minted into a
build running elsewhere.

members.name: permission
members.doc:
Narrow the token to one permission, e.g. `.permission("contents", "write")`.
Repeatable. Without any, the token holds the installation's whole grant,
which is the App's configured permissions — the sane default for an App
set up for one job. A hyphenated name is accepted as the mint accepts it.

members.name: fallback
members.doc:
The token yielded when no App is configured or the mint fails. Defaults
to `GITHUB_TOKEN` from the environment — the workflow's own token, so a
build that names an App still posts, as `github-actions[bot]`, wherever
the App is absent.

members.name: base_url
members.doc: Use a different REST base for the mint (GitHub Enterprise Server).

symbols.name: GhReleaseEnsureSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for ensuring a release exists.

`owner/repo` and the token fall back to the Actions environment, so a job
that already has them names only the release.

members.name: tag
members.doc:
The tag to release (required).

It should already exist. GitHub creates a missing tag on the default
branch rather than refusing, so a typo here publishes a tag as well as a
release — which is why the caller that reconciles a backlog reads its tags
from git rather than composing them.

members.name: name
members.doc: The release title (required), e.g. `Zuke Build v1.2.3`.

members.name: body
members.doc: The release notes (required); pass `""` for a release with none.

members.name: latest
members.doc:
Move the repository's "Latest release" pointer onto this release.

Off unless asked, which is the opposite of GitHub's own default — it
treats a new release as latest unless told otherwise. The default is
inverted because the first thing this is used for is back-filling
releases a pipeline missed, and those are created oldest-first: taking
GitHub's default would walk the pointer backwards through the backlog and
leave it on whichever release was created last, which is the oldest one.
Naming it explicitly costs the one caller that wants it a method call, and
costs the ones that do not want it nothing at all.

members.doc: `owner/repo`. Defaults to `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`.

members.name: token
members.doc: The token to authenticate with — needs `contents: write`. Defaults to `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

members.name: base_url
members.doc: The API root, for GitHub Enterprise.

members.name: app_token
members.signature: static async app_token(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhAppTokenSettings], GhAppTokenSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Mint a GitHub App installation token, scoped to the repositories and
permissions the settings request. The returned token is registered with the
Actions log masker, so it is safe to pass onward through `env`.

members.name: app_token_source
members.signature: static async app_token_source(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhAppTokenSourceSettings], GhAppTokenSourceSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
A token **source** for the App: a function that mints the installation
token the first time it is called and returns the same token after, or
yields `GITHUB_TOKEN` when the App is not configured — the credential a
build hands to an AI reviewer's `.commentToken(...)` so its reviews post
as the App where it is installed and as `github-actions[bot]` everywhere
else. Nothing runs until the first call.

``ts
appId = parameter("GitHub App id").env("REVIEW_APP_ID");
appKey = parameter("GitHub App key").secret().env("REVIEW_APP_KEY");
botToken = GhTasks.appTokenSource((s) => s.app(this.appId, this.appKey));
``

members.name: upload_sarif
members.signature: static async upload_sarif(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhSarifSettings], GhSarifSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Upload a SARIF report to GitHub code scanning, so its findings land in the
repository's Security tab. Needs a token with `security-events: write`.

members.name: upload_release_asset
members.signature: static async upload_release_asset(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhReleaseAssetSettings], GhReleaseAssetSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Attach a file to a GitHub release — the latest release by default, or the
one named by `.tag(...)`. Idempotent: an asset the release already
carries under the same name is kept as-is (unless `.refresh()` asks for
one with different bytes to be replaced), and a repository with no
releases resolves to `state: "no-release"` rather than throwing. Needs a
token with `contents: write`.

members.name: mark_release_latest
members.signature: static async mark_release_latest(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhReleaseLatestSettings], GhReleaseLatestSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Point the repository's "Latest release" at the release for `.tag(...)`.

Idempotent, and quiet about it: a pointer already on the tag's release is
left untouched rather than re-written, so an unattended pipeline can run
this unconditionally without churning the release's audit history. A tag
with no release resolves to `state: "no-release"` rather than throwing —
the release may be cut by a later, human step — while a tag that does not
exist at all is an error, because the caller named it. Needs a token with
`contents: write`.

members.name: ensure_release
members.signature: static async ensure_release(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhReleaseEnsureSettings], GhReleaseEnsureSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Publish a release for `.tag(...)` unless it already has one.

Reads the tag's release first and returns `state: "exists"` when there is
one, writing nothing — so an unattended pipeline can run this on every
push without overwriting notes a maintainer wrote by hand. Needs a token
with `contents: write`.

members.name: create_or_update_file
members.signature: static async create_or_update_file(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[GhContentsSettings], GhContentsSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Write one file through the contents API, creating it or replacing its
content — or, when it already holds exactly this content, writing nothing
and reporting `unchanged`.

A write that loses a race (the file changed between the read and the
write) is read once more: if the file now holds this content the result is
`unchanged`, otherwise the conflict is raised rather than overwritten.

packages.name: zuke.tools.git
packages.summary: `@zuke/git` 1.6.0: `@zuke/git` — typed `git` task wrappers for Zuke builds.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Paths/pathspecs to stage (positional); repeatable.

members.name: all
members.doc: Stage all changes including new files (`-A`/`--all`).

members.name: update
members.doc: Stage modifications and deletions, but not new files (`-u`/`--update`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Stage files git would otherwise ignore (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: intent_to_add
members.doc:
Record the paths' existence but not their contents (`-N`/`--intent-to-add`),
which is what makes an untracked file show up in `git diff`.

members.name: patches
members.doc: The patch files to apply (positional); repeatable. Reads stdin when empty.

members.name: check
members.doc: Report whether the patch would apply, changing nothing (`--check`).

members.name: reverse
members.doc: Apply the patch backwards (`--reverse`).

members.name: three_way
members.doc:
Fall back to a three-way merge when the patch does not apply cleanly
(`--3way`), leaving conflict markers instead of refusing outright.

members.name: index
members.doc: Apply to the index as well as the working tree (`--index`).

members.name: cached
members.doc: Apply to the index only, leaving the working tree alone (`--cached`).

members.name: strip
members.doc: Strip this many leading path components (`-p<n>`); git's default is 1.

members.name: whitespace
members.doc:
What to do about whitespace errors (`--whitespace=<action>`): `nowarn`,
`warn`, `fix`, `error`, or `error-all`.

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Skip files matching this pattern (`--exclude=<pattern>`); repeatable.

members.name: treeish
members.doc: The tree, commit, or tag to archive (positional, required).

members.name: format
members.doc: The archive format (`--format=<fmt>`), e.g. `tar`, `tar.gz`, or `zip`.

members.name: output
members.doc: Write to this file (`--output=<file>`) instead of stdout.

members.name: prefix
members.doc: Prepend this path to every entry (`--prefix=<prefix>/`).

members.name: remote
members.doc: Ask a remote repository for the archive (`--remote=<repo>`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Archive only these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

members.name: file
members.doc: The file to annotate (positional).

members.name: porcelain
members.doc:
Machine-readable output (`--porcelain`). Prefer
"./git.ts".GitTasks.blameLines, which parses it.

members.name: line_porcelain
members.doc:
Like porcelain, but repeating the commit header on every line
(`--line-porcelain`) rather than only its first appearance.

members.name: revision
members.doc: Annotate the file as of this revision (positional).

members.name: line_range
members.signature: line_range(start: float, end: float | str) -> Self
members.doc: Annotate only these lines (`-L <start>,<end>`); repeatable.

members.name: show_email
members.doc: Show the author's email rather than their name (`-e`).

members.name: ignore_whitespace
members.doc: Ignore whitespace-only changes when assigning blame (`-w`).

members.name: reverse
members.doc: Walk history forward from this revision instead (`--reverse <rev>`).

members.name: ignore_revs
members.doc: Ignore a revision when assigning blame (`--ignore-rev`); repeatable.

members.name: name
members.doc: The branch name to create or operate on.

members.name: start_point
members.doc:
The commit a created branch forks from (git's trailing `<start-point>`),
e.g. `origin/main`.

members.name: delete_branch
members.doc: Delete the branch (`-d`, or `-D` when forced).

members.name: rename
members.signature: rename(new_name: str, force: bool | None=None) -> Self
members.doc: Rename name to `newName` (`-m`, or `-M` when forced).

members.name: set_upstream_to
members.doc: Point the branch's upstream at this ref (`--set-upstream-to=<ref>`).

members.name: all
members.doc: List both local and remote-tracking branches (`-a`/`--all`).

members.name: remotes
members.doc: List remote-tracking branches only (`-r`/`--remotes`).

members.name: contains
members.doc: List only branches containing this commit (`--contains <commit>`).

members.name: merged
members.doc:
List only branches already merged into this ref (`--merged <ref>`) — the
listing a cleanup target filters stale branches from.

members.name: format
members.doc:
Render a listing through a format string (`--format=<fmt>`), e.g.
`%(refname:short)` for bare branch names with no `*` marker or padding.

members.name: sort
members.doc: Order a listing (`--sort=<key>`), e.g. `-committerdate` for most recent first.

members.name: object
members.doc: The object to read (positional), e.g. `"HEAD:deno.json"`.

members.name: query
members.doc:
Report an attribute rather than the contents: `type` (`-t`), `size`
(`-s`), or `exists` (`-e`, which answers by exit status and prints
nothing).

members.name: textconv
members.doc: Run the object through its textconv filter (`--textconv`).

members.name: filters
members.doc: Run the object through its working-tree filters (`--filters`).

members.name: quiet_output
members.doc:
Say nothing and answer by exit status alone (`-q`).

Named apart from the inherited `quiet`, which silences Zuke's echo of the
command rather than git's output.

members.name: verbose
members.doc: Also report the rule that excluded each path (`-v`).

members.name: non_matching
members.doc: Include the paths that are *not* excluded (`-n`); needs verbose.

members.name: no_index
members.doc: Ignore the index when checking (`--no-index`).

members.name: nul_terminated
members.doc: Terminate records with NUL rather than newline (`-z`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: The paths to check (positional); repeatable.

members.name: ref
members.doc:
The branch or commit to check out — or, with paths, the source to
restore those paths from. Required unless paths is given.

members.name: paths
members.doc:
Restore one or more paths (`git checkout [<ref>] -- <paths>`). The `--`
separates paths from any ref so a path is never misread as a branch name;
repeatable. With no ref, restores the paths from the index
(discarding working-tree changes).

members.name: create
members.doc: Create a new branch (`-b`).

members.name: detach
members.doc: Check the ref out with a detached `HEAD` (`--detach`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Force checkout, discarding local changes (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: allow_empty
members.doc: Keep a commit that produces no changes (`--allow-empty`).

members.name: ff
members.doc: Fast-forward instead of rewriting when the parent matches `HEAD` (`--ff`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the clean to these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

members.name: force
members.doc: Actually delete the files (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: dry_run
members.doc: List what would be deleted without deleting it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

members.name: directories
members.doc: Also remove untracked directories (`-d`).

members.name: include_ignored
members.doc:
Remove ignored files too (`-x`) — the switch that turns a clean into a
from-scratch build, since `node_modules` and `target/` are ignored.

members.name: only_ignored
members.doc: Remove *only* ignored files (`-X`), keeping other untracked ones.

members.name: exclude
members.doc: Spare paths matching this pattern (`--exclude=<pattern>`); repeatable.

members.name: repository
members.doc: The repository URL to clone (required).

members.name: directory
members.doc: Target directory for the clone.

members.name: branch
members.doc: Check out a specific branch (`-b`/`--branch`).

members.name: depth
members.doc: Create a shallow clone of the given depth (`--depth`).

members.name: bare
members.doc: Clone a bare repository (`--bare`).

members.name: filter
members.doc:
Partial-clone filter (`--filter=<spec>`), e.g. `blob:none` for a treeless
clone that fetches blobs on demand — the cheap way to get full history in
CI without the file contents of every revision.

members.name: single_branch
members.doc: Clone only the history of the checked-out branch (`--single-branch`).

members.name: recurse_submodules
members.doc: Also clone submodules (`--recurse-submodules`).

members.name: message
members.doc: The commit message (`-m`).

members.name: all
members.doc: Stage modified/deleted files before committing (`-a`/`--all`).

members.name: amend
members.doc: Amend the previous commit (`--amend`).

members.name: no_edit
members.doc: Keep the existing message when amending (`--no-edit`).

members.name: allow_empty
members.doc: Allow a commit with no changes (`--allow-empty`).

members.name: no_verify
members.doc:
Skip the `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` hooks (`--no-verify`) — what a bot
commit wants when the hooks are meant for humans at a terminal.

members.name: author
members.doc: Attribute the commit to someone else (`--author="Name <email>"`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Commit only these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

symbols.name: GitConfigSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `git config`. Pick the operation with get,
getAll, set, add, unset, or list,
and the file with global, local, system,
worktree, or file.

members.name: get
members.doc: Read a key's value (`--get <key>`).

members.name: get_all
members.doc: Read every value of a multi-valued key (`--get-all <key>`).

members.name: set
members.doc: Set a key, replacing any existing value (`git config <key> <value>`).

members.name: add
members.doc: Add another value to a multi-valued key (`--add <key> <value>`).

members.name: unset
members.doc: Remove a key (`--unset <key>`).

members.name: list
members.doc: List every configured key (`--list`).

members.name: global_
members.doc: Use the user's configuration (`--global`).

members.name: local
members.doc: Use the repository's configuration (`--local`).

members.name: system
members.doc: Use the machine's configuration (`--system`).

members.name: worktree
members.doc: Use the worktree's configuration (`--worktree`).

members.name: file
members.doc: Use a specific file (`--file <path>`), rather than one of the scopes.

members.name: default_value
members.doc:
What to report when the key is unset (`--default <value>`), which also
makes `--get` exit 0 instead of 1.

symbols.name: GitDefaultBranchSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for "./git.ts".GitTasks.defaultBranch: which remote to ask,
plus the global options every git task shares.

members.name: remote
members.doc: The remote whose default branch is wanted (default `origin`).

members.name: commitish
members.doc: The commit to describe (positional); defaults to `HEAD`.

members.name: tags
members.doc: Consider lightweight tags too, not only annotated ones (`--tags`).

members.name: all
members.doc: Consider every ref, not only tags (`--all`).

members.name: always
members.doc: Fall back to an abbreviated SHA when no tag matches (`--always`).

members.name: exact_match
members.doc: Fail unless the commit is exactly at a tag (`--exact-match`).

members.name: abbrev
members.doc:
How many SHA characters to append (`--abbrev=<n>`). `0` suppresses the
suffix entirely, which is how a build reads the nearest tag's bare name.

members.name: dirty
members.doc: Append a marker when the working tree is dirty (`--dirty[=<suffix>]`).

members.name: match_
members.doc: Only consider tags matching this glob (`--match <pattern>`); repeatable.

members.name: commits
members.doc:
The commits to compare (positional); repeatable. One rev diffs the working
tree against it; two diff them against each other.

members.name: merge_base
members.signature: merge_base(from_: str, to: str | None=None) -> Self
members.doc:
Compare the two ends of a range — `from...to` with three dots, which diffs
`to` against the point the two branches last shared. That is the diff a
pull request shows, and the one a review or an "affected" check wants,
since it excludes whatever landed on the base branch meanwhile.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the diff to these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

members.name: staged
members.doc: Diff the index against `HEAD` rather than the working tree (`--staged`).

members.name: name_only
members.doc: List the changed paths instead of the patch (`--name-only`).

members.name: name_status
members.doc: List the changed paths with their status letters (`--name-status`).

members.name: stat
members.doc: Summarise the changes per file (`--stat`).

members.name: shortstat
members.doc: One summary line for the whole diff (`--shortstat`).

members.name: unified
members.doc: Lines of context around each hunk (`--unified=<n>`).

members.name: ignore_all_space
members.doc: Ignore whitespace entirely when comparing (`--ignore-all-space`).

members.name: exit_code
members.doc:
Report differences through the exit code (`--exit-code`): 1 when there are
any, 0 when there are none. Pair it with `.noThrow()` to branch on
`output.code` instead of catching.

members.name: diff_filter
members.doc:
Keep only files whose change matches these status letters
(`--diff-filter=<letters>`), e.g. `ACM` for added, copied, and modified —
how a lint target skips paths the diff only deleted.

members.name: nul_terminated
members.doc: Terminate output records with a NUL rather than a newline (`-z`).

members.name: remote
members.doc: The remote to fetch from.

members.name: refspec
members.doc:
Add a refspec to fetch, after the remote — `master`, or
`master:refs/remotes/origin/master` to also update the remote-tracking ref
(which is what makes `origin/master` resolvable in a shallow CI checkout
that never fetched it). Repeatable.

Prefix the source with `+` to force the update. Pair it with
depth: a shallow fetch is not a fast-forward of the history
already present, and git rejects such an update unless it is forced.

members.name: no_tags
members.doc: Skip fetching tags (`--no-tags`).

members.name: depth
members.doc:
Limit history to this many commits (`--depth`). `1` is enough to diff
against a base branch and avoids pulling a whole history into a CI job.

members.name: unshallow
members.doc:
Deepen a shallow clone into the full history (`--unshallow`) — what a
release target needs before `git describe` or a changelog can see past the
one commit CI checked out.

members.name: all
members.doc: Fetch from all remotes (`--all`).

members.name: tags
members.doc: Also fetch tags (`--tags`).

members.name: prune
members.doc: Prune deleted remote refs (`--prune`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Update refs even when the update is not a fast-forward (`--force`).

members.name: format
members.doc: The output format (`--format=<format>`), in git's placeholder language.

members.name: ignore_case

members.name: omit_empty

members.name: ignore_case

members.name: oneline

members.name: since

Exit non-zero when a pathspec matches nothing (`--error-unmatch`), which

git only applies it to the paths it was given, so it needs
paths — the flag on its own describes a whole-tree listing, which
always matches something.

members.name: nul_terminated

members.name: remote

members.name: patterns

members.name: heads

members.name: tags

members.name: refs

members.name: exit_code

members.name: trees_only

members.name: nul_terminated
members.doc: Terminate entries with NUL rather than newline (`-z`).

members.name: name_only

members.name: object_only

members.name: full_name

members.name: full_tree

members.name: abbrev

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the listing to these paths (positional); repeatable.

members.name: all

members.name: independent

members.name: fork_point

members.name: commits
members.doc: The commits to consider (positional); repeatable.

members.name: refs

members.name: message
members.doc: The merge commit's message (`-m`).

members.name: no_ff
members.doc: Always create a merge commit (`--no-ff`), even when a fast-forward would do.

members.name: ff_only
members.doc: Refuse anything but a fast-forward (`--ff-only`).

members.name: squash
members.doc: Stage the merged result without recording a merge (`--squash`).

members.name: no_commit
members.doc: Merge but leave the commit to the caller (`--no-commit`).

members.name: strategy
members.doc: The merge strategy (`--strategy=<name>`), e.g. `ours`.

members.name: strategy_option
allow_unrelated_histories
members.doc: Merge histories that share no commit (`--allow-unrelated-histories`).

members.name: write_tree
members.doc:
Do a real merge and write the resulting tree (`--write-tree`), rather than
the trivial three-way form. This is the default in git 2.38 and later.

members.name: messages
members.doc: Also print the informational and conflict messages (`--messages`).

members.name: name_only
members.doc: List conflicted filenames without modes or object names (`--name-only`).

members.name: nul_terminated
members.doc: Separate paths with NUL rather than newline (`-z`).

members.name: allow_unrelated_histories
members.doc: Permit merging histories with no common ancestor (`--allow-unrelated-histories`).

members.name: merge_base
members.doc: Use this commit as the merge base (`--merge-base=<commit>`).

members.name: branches
members.doc: The two branches to merge (positional).

members.name: sources
members.doc: The path(s) to move (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: destination
members.doc:
Where they move to (required): a file name for a single source, a
directory when there is more than one.

members.name: force
members.doc: Overwrite an existing destination (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: dry_run
members.doc: Report what would move without moving it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

members.name: tags
members.doc: Use only tags to name the commits (`--tags`).

members.name: all
members.doc: Name every reachable commit (`--all`).

members.name: name_only
members.doc: Print only the name, not the commit it names (`--name-only`).

members.name: always_name
members.doc: Fall back to the object name when nothing else names it (`--always`).

members.name: refs
members.doc: Only consider refs matching these patterns (`--refs=<pattern>`).

members.name: commits
members.doc: The commits to name (positional); repeatable.

members.name: remote
members.doc: The remote to pull from.

members.name: ref
members.doc: The refspec/branch to pull.

members.name: rebase
members.doc: Rebase instead of merge (`--rebase`).

members.name: no_rebase
members.doc:
Merge rather than rebase (`--no-rebase`), whatever `pull.rebase` is set to
in the ambient config — the flag a build reaches for when it must not
depend on the machine it runs on.

members.name: ff_only
members.doc: Only fast-forward (`--ff-only`).

members.name: depth
members.doc: Limit the fetched history to this many commits (`--depth`).

members.name: tags
members.doc: Also fetch tags (`--tags`).

members.name: prune
members.doc: Prune deleted remote refs while fetching (`--prune`).

members.name: remote
members.doc: The remote to push to (e.g. `origin`).

members.name: ref
members.doc: The refspec/branch to push.

members.name: set_upstream
members.doc: Set the upstream tracking ref (`-u`/`--set-upstream`).

members.name: tags
members.doc: Also push tags (`--tags`).

members.name: follow_tags
members.doc:
Push the annotated tags reachable from the refs being pushed
(`--follow-tags`) — a release target's tag rides along with its commit
instead of needing a second push.

members.name: force_with_lease
members.doc: Force push, but only if the remote ref is unchanged (`--force-with-lease`).

members.name: delete_ref
members.doc: Delete the remote ref (`--delete`).

members.name: atomic
members.doc: Update every ref or none (`--atomic`).

members.name: dry_run
members.doc: Report what would be pushed without pushing it (`--dry-run`).

members.name: push_option
members.doc:
Send a server-side option (`--push-option=<value>`); repeatable. GitLab
reads these for `ci.skip` and merge-request creation.

members.name: upstream

members.name: keep_empty

symbols.name: GitRemoteSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `git remote`. Pick the subcommand with list,
add, remove, rename, setUrl,
getUrl, show, or prune.

members.name: list
members.doc: List the configured remotes (`git remote`), the default.

members.name: add
members.doc: Add a remote (`git remote add <name> <url>`).

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove a remote and its tracking refs (`git remote remove <name>`).

members.name: rename
members.doc: Rename a remote (`git remote rename <old> <new>`).

members.name: set_url
members.doc:
Change a remote's URL (`git remote set-url <name> <url>`). Add
pushUrl to change only the push URL.

members.name: get_url
members.doc: Print a remote's URL (`git remote get-url <name>`).

members.name: show
members.doc: Describe a remote and its branches (`git remote show <name>`).

members.name: prune
members.doc: Delete tracking refs the remote no longer has (`git remote prune <name>`).

members.name: verbose
members.doc: Show each remote's URLs when listing (`-v`/`--verbose`).

members.name: fetch
members.doc: Fetch from the remote right after adding it (`-f`, `add` only).

members.name: track
members.doc: Track only this branch (`-t <branch>`, `add` only).

members.name: push_url
members.doc: Operate on the push URL (`--push`), for setUrl and getUrl.

symbols.name: GitReplaySettings
symbols.doc:
Shared base for `cherry-pick` and `revert`: the same commit list, the same
`--no-commit`/`--mainline`, and the same four control flags. Only the
subcommand's name and the extra flags differ, which is why they are one
implementation rather than two that drift.

members.name: commits
members.doc: The commits to replay (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: no_commit
members.doc: Apply the change without committing it (`-n`/`--no-commit`).

members.name: mainline
members.doc:
Which parent of a merge commit to treat as the mainline
(`-m <parent-number>`), counting from 1. Replaying a merge needs it: git
cannot otherwise tell which side of the merge the change is.

members.name: signoff
members.doc: Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer (`--signoff`).

members.name: skip
members.doc: Drop the current commit and carry on (`--skip`).

members.name: ref
members.doc: The commit to reset to (positional); defaults to `HEAD`.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Reset only these pathspecs — unstaging them (positional); repeatable.

members.name: soft
members.doc: Move the branch only, keeping the index and working tree (`--soft`).

members.name: mixed
members.doc: Reset the index but not the working tree (`--mixed`), git's default.

members.name: hard
members.doc: Reset the index *and* the working tree (`--hard`), discarding changes.

members.name: merge
members.doc: Reset, keeping changes to files that differ between the commits (`--merge`).

members.name: keep
members.doc: Like merge, but refuse when a changed file differs (`--keep`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: The pathspecs to restore (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: source
members.doc:
Restore the contents from this commit or tree (`--source=<tree-ish>`)
rather than from the index.

members.name: staged
members.doc:
Restore the index (`--staged`) — unstaging the paths. Combine with
worktree to reset both, which is what `git restore -SW` does.

members.name: worktree
members.doc: Restore the working tree (`--worktree`), git's default when neither is given.

members.name: no_edit
members.doc: Take the generated message without opening an editor (`--no-edit`).

members.name: count
members.doc:
Print how many commits the walk found rather than listing them
(`--count`). Prefer "./git.ts".GitTasks.commitCount, which reads
that number back.

members.name: max_count
members.doc: Stop after this many commits (`--max-count=<n>`).

members.name: skip
members.doc: Skip this many commits before printing (`--skip=<n>`).

members.name: all
members.doc: Walk every ref in `refs/` (`--all`).

members.name: branches
members.doc: Walk every branch (`--branches`).

members.name: tags
members.doc: Walk every tag (`--tags`).

members.name: remotes
members.doc: Walk every remote-tracking branch (`--remotes`).

members.name: no_merges
members.doc: Omit merge commits (`--no-merges`).

members.name: merges
members.doc: Keep only merge commits (`--merges`).

members.name: first_parent
members.doc: Follow only the first parent of each merge (`--first-parent`).

members.name: reverse
members.doc: Emit the commits oldest first (`--reverse`).

members.name: topo_order
members.doc: Order by topology rather than date (`--topo-order`).

members.name: date_order
members.doc: Order by commit date (`--date-order`).

members.name: since
members.doc: Only commits after this date (`--since=<date>`).

members.name: until
members.doc: Only commits before this date (`--until=<date>`).

members.name: author
members.doc: Only commits whose author matches (`--author=<pattern>`).

members.name: commits
members.doc:
The commits or ranges to walk (positional), e.g. `"HEAD"` or
`"origin/main..HEAD"`; repeatable.

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the walk to commits touching these paths (positional); repeatable.

members.name: rev
members.doc: The revisions or arguments to resolve (positional); repeatable.

members.name: short
members.doc:
Abbreviate the SHA (`--short`, or `--short=<n>` with a length). git picks
a length long enough to stay unambiguous when none is given.

members.name: abbrev_ref
members.doc: Print the ref's short name (`--abbrev-ref`), e.g. `main` for `HEAD`.

members.name: verify
members.doc: Fail rather than echo the argument when it names no object (`--verify`).

members.name: git_dir
members.doc: Print the path of the `.git` directory (`--git-dir`).

members.name: show_toplevel
members.doc: Print the absolute path of the working tree's root (`--show-toplevel`).

members.name: show_prefix
members.doc: Print the current directory's path relative to that root (`--show-prefix`).

members.name: is_inside_work_tree
members.doc: Print whether this is inside a working tree (`--is-inside-work-tree`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Paths/pathspecs to remove (positional, required); repeatable.

members.name: cached
members.doc:
Remove from the index only, leaving the file on disk (`--cached`) — how a

members.name: recursive
members.doc: Recurse into directories (`-r`).

members.name: force
members.doc: Remove even when the file has staged or local changes (`-f`/`--force`).

members.name: dry_run
members.doc: Report what would be removed without removing it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

members.name: ignore_unmatch
members.doc: Exit 0 when no path matches (`--ignore-unmatch`).

symbols.name: GitRunSettings

symbols.name: GitSequencerSettings
symbols.doc:
Base for the commands that can be left in progress by a conflict. Subclasses

members.name: quit
members.doc: Forget the operation, leaving the tree as it is (`--quit`).

symbols.name: GitSettings
symbols.doc: Shared base for every `git` subcommand: the binary and global options.

members.name: dir
members.doc: Run git as if started in `path` (`-C <path>`).

members.name: config
members.doc: Set a one-off config value (`-c key=value`); repeatable.

members.name: summary
members.doc:
Report only the commit count per author, without the subjects (`-s`).

output back.

members.name: numbered
members.doc: Sort by commit count rather than by name (`-n`).

members.name: email
members.doc: Include each author's email address (`-e`).

members.name: committer
members.doc: Group by committer rather than author (`-c`).

members.name: group
members.doc: Group by a named field (`--group=<field>`), e.g. `"trailer:co-authored-by"`.

members.name: commits

members.name: paths

members.name: tags

members.name: heads

members.name: head

members.name: dereference

members.name: hash

members.name: exists

Suppress git's own stdout (`--quiet`), leaving the exit status as the

members.name: patterns

members.name: paths

members.name: format
members.doc: Render the commit header through a format string (`--format=<fmt>`).

members.name: no_patch
members.doc: Suppress the diff (`--no-patch`), leaving only the header.

members.name: name_only
members.doc: List the changed paths instead of the diff (`--name-only`).

members.name: name_status

members.name: stat
members.doc: Summarise the changes (`--stat`).

symbols.name: GitStashSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `git stash`. Pick the subcommand with push,
pop, apply, list, show, drop, or
clear; the remaining methods apply to the one picked.

members.name: push
members.doc: Stash the working tree and index (`git stash push`).

members.name: pop
members.doc: Restore a stash and drop it (`git stash pop`).

members.name: apply
members.doc: Restore a stash and keep it (`git stash apply`).

members.name: list
members.doc: List the stashes (`git stash list`).

members.name: show
members.doc: Show a stash's diff (`git stash show`).

members.name: drop
members.doc: Discard a stash (`git stash drop`).

members.name: clear
members.doc: Discard every stash (`git stash clear`).

members.name: stash
members.doc:
Which stash to act on, e.g. `stash@{1}` (positional); defaults to the most
recent. Only meaningful for pop, apply, show, and
drop.

members.name: message
members.doc: Label the stash being pushed (`-m`).

members.name: include_untracked
members.doc: Stash untracked files too (`--include-untracked`).

members.name: keep_index
members.doc: Leave what is already staged in the index (`--keep-index`).

members.name: staged
members.doc: Stash only what is staged (`--staged`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Stash only these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

members.name: short
members.doc: Short-format output (`-s`/`--short`).

members.name: porcelain
members.doc: Stable machine-readable output (`--porcelain`).

members.name: branch
members.doc: Show branch information (`-b`/`--branch`).

members.name: nul_terminated
members.doc:
Terminate each record with a NUL rather than a newline (`-z`), which also
turns on `--porcelain` and stops git quoting unusual paths.

members.name: untracked_files
members.doc:
How much of an untracked directory to report (`--untracked-files=<mode>`):
`no`, `normal` (the default — the directory), or `all` (every file in it).

members.name: ignored
members.doc: Also report ignored files (`--ignored`).

members.name: paths
members.doc: Limit the report to these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

symbols.doc:

symbols.name: GitWorktreeSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for `git worktree`. Pick the subcommand with add,
list, remove, or prune; the remaining methods apply
to the one picked, mirroring the flags git accepts for it.

members.name: add
members.doc: Check a new worktree out at `path` (`git worktree add <path>`).

members.name: list
members.doc: List the repository's worktrees (`git worktree list`).

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove the worktree at `path` (`git worktree remove <path>`).

members.name: prune
members.doc: Discard records of worktrees whose directories are gone (`git worktree prune`).

members.name: branch
members.doc:
The branch to check out in the new worktree — or, with
createBranch, the name of the branch to create there.

members.name: create_branch
members.doc: Create branch rather than checking out an existing one (`-b`).

members.name: start_point
members.doc:
The commit the new branch forks from — git's trailing `<commit-ish>`, e.g.
`origin/main`. Only meaningful with createBranch: without a start
point git branches from the *parent* checkout's `HEAD`, which is whatever
the developer happened to have open.

Setting this and branch without createBranch is refused:
both want the same trailing position, and there is no reading of the
command where git would take them both.

members.name: detach
members.doc: Check out with a detached `HEAD` (`--detach`).

members.name: force
members.doc:
Force the operation (`--force`): check out a branch already checked out
elsewhere, or remove a worktree with modifications. Without it git refuses
both.

members.name: porcelain
members.doc: Emit the stable machine-readable listing (`--porcelain`).

The service-account key and every token signed with it stay out of progress
lines and errors. Declare the key in the build as `parameter(...).secret()`
so Zuke masks it in its own output too.

members.doc:

(or Google Cloud) downloaded; required. The account needs the *Release
apps to testing tracks* (or *Release to production*) permission on the
app.

members.doc: The app's package name, e.g. `com.example.app`; required.

members.name: bundle
members.doc: The Android app bundle (`.aab`) to upload; required.

members.name: track
members.doc:
The track to release on: `internal` (the default), `alpha`, `beta`,
`production`, or the name of a closed testing track.

members.doc:
Commit without sending the changes for review, so an app with managed

symbols.doc: Settings for a formula that installs prebuilt binaries.

members.doc:
The formula name (required), e.g. `app` or `app@2`: a lowercase letter,
then lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `+` or `@`. The Ruby class
name is derived from it exactly as Homebrew does — `app-cli` defines
`AppCli`, `app@2` defines `AppAT2`.

members.name: description
members.doc:
The one-line description (`desc`, required), held to `brew audit`'s rules:
at most 80 characters, starting with a capital letter, not with an
article or the formula's name, and with no trailing period.

members.name: homepage
members.doc: The project's homepage (required; must be `https`).

members.name: version
members.doc:
The version, e.g. `1.2.3` — set it only when Homebrew cannot read it from
the archive URLs.

Homebrew detects a formula's version from its URL, and `brew audit`
rejects a `version` line that repeats what it detected ("version … is
redundant with version scanned from URL"). A GitHub release asset such as
`…/releases/download/v1.2.3/app-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` carries it, so
leave this unset there; `expectVersion()` in the test still works, against
the detected version. Set it for a URL with no version in it, such as a
`…/releases/latest/download/…` link or a content-addressed store.

at least one is required, and each OS/arch pair at most once.

the child's argv, where `ps` and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` expose it to every
other user on the host and to every process the build starts. There is no
environment variable to move it to.

On GitHub Actions, prefer OIDC and pass no token at all: the publish is
authenticated by the workflow's identity, so there is no credential to
expose. This is for the cases where that is not available.

symbols.name: NodeEvaluateSettings
symbols.doc:
Settings for "./node.ts".NodeTasks.evaluate — which export of the
module to take, and what to call it with.

members.name: export
members.doc:
The named export to take, instead of the default one.

The export is awaited; when it is a function it is called first, with
callWith's arguments.

members.name: call_with
members.doc:
Arguments for the exported function, in order. Each must be
JSON-serialisable — they cross a process boundary as JSON.

Named `callWith` rather than `args` because `ToolSettings.args` already
means "append raw arguments to the `node` command line", which is a
different thing.

members.name: exit_after_result
members.doc:
End the Node process as soon as the result has been written, instead of
waiting for the module to let Node exit on its own.

A module that leaves a live handle on the event loop — an HTTP server, a
database pool, a timer — never exits, and the evaluation then blocks
forever on a value it has *already* produced and written. This makes the
driver exit once that write has flushed, so such a module can be evaluated
as it is, without a `process.exit` of its own.

What the module does *after* handing back its value does not happen. The
process ends at the write, so anything it would still print is cut off,
anything it would still do — a `beforeExit` handler, a teardown scheduled
on the next tick, a flush that has not been awaited — does not run, and its
own exit code is no longer observed (the driver exits `0`). That is the
trade the option makes, and why it is opt-in rather than the default:
choose it for a module whose value is the whole point of running it, and
whose remaining work is process teardown the operating system is about to
do anyway. A module whose after-the-value work *matters* — one that writes
a file, commits a transaction, or reports its own failure through an exit
code — should keep the default and be given a way to exit on its own.

Two shapes are unaffected either way: a module that throws before producing
a result still rejects the evaluation, since the driver never reaches its
final write, and a module that exits on its own never notices the option.

members.name: evaluate
members.signature: static async evaluate(ctx: ServiceContext, module: str, configure: Callable[[NodeEvaluateSettings], NodeEvaluateSettings] | None=None) -> object
members.doc:
Import a Node module and resolve to one of its exports' JSON value — the
way a target reads something *out* of the Node side of a project (an
OpenAPI document, a resolved config) instead of shelling out to a script
that has to write it somewhere first.

`module` is a path, resolved against the working directory. The export
(`default` unless NodeEvaluateSettings.export names another) is
awaited; when it is a function it is called with
NodeEvaluateSettings.callWith's arguments first.

``ts
// tools/openapi.mjs: export default async () => document
const spec = await NodeTasks.evaluate("tools/openapi.mjs");
``

The evaluation waits for the Node process to exit, so a module that leaves
a live handle on the event loop (a server, a pool, a timer) would block on
a value it has already produced. NodeEvaluateSettings.exitAfterResult
ends the process as soon as the result has been written, for modules in
that shape.

The module runs as a real Node process with the build's own permissions —
the same trust level as a script handed to NodeTasks.run, and the
reason this is a build-authoring API rather than an input-processing one.
`module` is code: build it from a literal or from the project's own layout,
never from an untrusted source (a pull request title, a webhook payload),
exactly as for every other command a build spawns. Values passed through
NodeEvaluateSettings.callWith cannot inject into the driver — they

members.doc: List this account's tokens (`token list`), the default.

members.name: create
members.doc: Create a token (`token create`).

members.name: revoke
members.doc:
Revoke a token by id or value (`token revoke <id|token>`).

npm takes this positionally, with no environment route, so the value
reaches the child's argv either way. It is registered with the run's
redactor so every *rendering* of the command masks it; the process table
is not something the wrapper can do anything about here.

Masked whichever it is, because the two are indistinguishable from here —
npm accepts the id or the token itself, and nothing in the string says
which. Masking an id costs a `[redacted]` in this run's output; not
masking a token puts a live credential in it.

packages.name: zuke.tools.prometheus
packages.summary: `@zuke/prometheus` 1.1.1: A typed client for the Prometheus HTTP API, for Zuke builds.

members.name: region
members.doc:
The workspace's region, such as `us-east-1`; defaults to `AWS_REGION`,
then `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`.

members.name: profile
members.doc:
Read static keys from this profile of the shared credentials and config
files (`~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.aws/config`) instead of searching the
default chain.

members.name: access_key
members.signature: access_key(access_key_id: str, secret_access_key: str, session_token: str | None=None) -> Self
members.doc: Sign with this access key instead of searching the default chain.

members.name: scope
members.doc: The scope to request, replacing `https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com/.default`.

members.name: tenant_id
members.doc: The Microsoft Entra tenant (directory) id; defaults to `AZURE_TENANT_ID`.

members.name: client_id
members.doc:
The application's client id — or, for a user-assigned managed identity,
the identity's; defaults to `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`.

members.name: authority_host
members.doc:
The Microsoft Entra authority, such as `https://login.microsoftonline.us`
for Azure Government; defaults to `AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST`, then
`https://login.microsoftonline.com`.

members.name: client_secret
members.doc:
Use a service principal's client secret (the client-credentials grant).
The secret defaults to `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`.

members.name: workload_identity
members.doc:
Use workload identity federation: the Kubernetes service-account token
in `tokenFile` (default `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`) is the client
assertion, read afresh on every token request since it is rotated.

members.name: managed_identity
members.doc:
Use the managed identity of the VM, App Service or Functions app the
build runs on. Pass a user-assigned identity's client id, or leave it
out for `clientId(...)` / `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, and failing those the
system-assigned identity.

symbols.name: PrometheusConnectionSettings
symbols.doc: The connection half of every Prometheus call's settings.

members.name: url
members.doc:
The Prometheus base URL, such as `https://prometheus.internal`. A path or
query string it carries — a proxy prefix, a tenant parameter — is kept,
and the endpoint path is appended. Userinfo in the URL
(`https://user:pass@host`) is taken off the URL and sent as basic auth.
When the call carries any credential — a configured source, or that
userinfo — the URL must be `https:` unless it is loopback, or
`ZUKE_ALLOW_INSECURE_URL` is set, since a plaintext request hands the
credential to anyone on the path. An unauthenticated URL may be plaintext,
as an in-cluster `http://prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090` usually is.

members.name: bearer_token
members.doc: Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

members.name: basic_auth
members.doc: Authenticate with HTTP basic auth (`Authorization: Basic …`).

members.name: header
members.doc:
Send a fixed header, such as a tenant id (`X-Scope-OrgID`). A plain
header does not make the call credentialed, so an in-cluster
`http://` Mimir, Cortex or Thanos with a tenant header keeps working —
except `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, and a name core's
URL redactor treats as credential-bearing (`X-API-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`:
names containing `key`, `token`, `secret`, `auth`, `pass` and the like),
which count as credentials. For an API key under any other name use
secretHeader. The value is masked in errors either way (when eight
or more characters long).

members.name: secret_header
members.doc:
Send a fixed header that carries a credential — an API key such as
`X-API-Key`. Like `bearerToken`, it makes the call credentialed, so the
URL must be `https:` unless it is loopback, and its value is masked in
errors.

members.name: google
members.doc:
Authenticate to Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus with an
OAuth access token from Application Default Credentials — no `gcloud`
needed. The search order is `credentialsFile(...)`, else the file
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` names; then gcloud's
`application_default_credentials.json`; then the GCE / GKE metadata
server. A file may be a `service_account` key, an `authorized_user`
gcloud login, or an `external_account` workload identity federation
configuration with a `file` or `url` subject-token source. The scope
defaults to `monitoring.read`; the token is cached until shortly before
it expires.

``ts
s.url("https://monitoring.googleapis.com/v1/projects/my-project/location/global/prometheus")
  .google()
``

members.name: azure
members.doc:
Authenticate to Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus with a
Microsoft Entra ID token for
`https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com/.default` — no `az` needed. Unless
a credential is chosen, the first the environment configures is used:
client secret (`AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`,
`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`), then workload identity (`AZURE_TENANT_ID`,
`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`), then managed identity
(App Service's `IDENTITY_ENDPOINT`, else the VM's IMDS). The token is
cached until shortly before it expires.

``ts
s.url("https://my-amw.eastus.prometheus.monitor.azure.com")
  .azure((a) => a.managedIdentity(clientId))
``

members.name: sigv4
members.doc:
Sign every request with AWS Signature Version 4 for Amazon Managed
Service for Prometheus (service `aps`) — no `aws` CLI needed. The region
is `region(...)`, else `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. Credentials
come from `accessKey(...)` or `profile(...)` when set, else the chain:
the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` environment, the shared files' profile, web
identity (`AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` + `AWS_ROLE_ARN`), the ECS / EKS
Pod Identity container endpoint, then EC2 IMDSv2. Configure it after any
other source, so it signs the headers they add.

``ts
s.url("https://aps-workspaces.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/workspaces/ws-1234")
  .sigv4((a) => a.region("us-east-1"))
``

members.name: request_timeout
members.doc:
How long the call may take, end to end (`"10s"`, or ms; default 30 s).
Client-side: the query's own `timeout` parameter is separate.

members.name: max_response_bytes
members.doc:
The largest response body to read, in bytes (default 64 MiB). A larger
one fails the call rather than being buffered whole.

symbols.name: PrometheusExpressionSettings
symbols.doc: What an instant and a range query share: the expression and its limits.

members.name: query
members.doc: The PromQL expression (`query`).

members.name: timeout
members.doc:
The evaluation timeout (`timeout`), such as `"30s"` — capped by the
server's `-query.timeout`. The client-side limit is `requestTimeout`.

members.name: limit
members.doc: The most series to return (`limit`); `0` means no limit.

members.name: lookback_delta
members.doc: Override the lookback period for this query (`lookback_delta`).

members.name: http_method
members.doc: Send the parameters as a `POST` form (the default) or in a `GET` URL.

members.name: scopes
members.doc:
The OAuth scopes to request, replacing the default
`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/monitoring.read`. A gcloud user
credential (`authorized_user`) carries the scopes it was granted at
`gcloud auth application-default login` and ignores these.

members.name: credentials_file
members.doc:
Read this credentials file — a service-account key, a gcloud user
credential, or a workload identity federation configuration — instead of
searching Application Default Credentials.

members.name: quota_project
members.doc:
The project charged for the request's quota, sent as
`x-goog-user-project`. Defaults to the credentials file's
`quota_project_id`, which `gcloud auth application-default
set-quota-project` writes.

members.name: http_method
members.doc: Send the parameters as a `POST` form (the default) or in a `GET` URL.

members.name: label_name
members.doc:
The label whose values to list. Any name is accepted: one outside the
classic `[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*` form (a UTF-8 name such as
`http.status_code`) is sent in the API's `U__` value-encoding escape, so
nothing in the name can reach the URL path as a separator.

members.name: limit
members.doc: The most metrics to return (`limit`).

members.name: limit_per_metric
members.doc: The most metadata entries per metric (`limit_per_metric`).

members.name: metric
members.doc: Only this metric's metadata (`metric`).

members.name: start
members.doc: The inclusive start (`start`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

members.name: end
members.doc: The inclusive end (`end`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

members.name: step
members.doc: The resolution step (`step`): `"15s"`, or a number of seconds.

members.name: time
members.doc: The evaluation time (`time`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

members.name: type_
members.doc: Only alerting (`"alert"`) or only recording (`"record"`) rules (`type`).

members.name: rule_name
members.doc: Only rules with these names (`rule_name[]`).

members.name: rule_group
members.doc: Only rules in these groups (`rule_group[]`).

members.name: file
members.doc: Only rules from these files (`file[]`).

members.name: match_
members.doc: Only rules whose configured labels match these selectors (`match[]`).

members.name: exclude_alerts
members.doc: Leave out each rule's active alerts (`exclude_alerts=true`).

members.name: group_limit
members.doc: At most this many rule groups per page (`group_limit`).

members.name: group_next_token
members.doc: Continue from a previous page's `groupNextToken` (`group_next_token`).

symbols.name: PrometheusSelectionSettings
symbols.doc: What the series, label-name and label-value endpoints share.

members.name: match_
members.doc: Add series selectors (`match[]`), such as `up` or `{job="api"}`.

members.name: start
members.doc: The start time (`start`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

members.name: end
members.doc: The end time (`end`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

members.name: limit
members.doc: The most results to return (`limit`); `0` means no limit.

symbols.name: PrometheusSeriesSettings
symbols.doc: Settings for finding series by matchers (`/api/v1/series`).

members.name: http_method
members.doc: Send the parameters as a `POST` form (the default) or in a `GET` URL.

members.name: state
members.doc: Only active or only dropped targets (`state`); both by default.

symbols.name: PrometheusTasks
symbols.doc:
The Prometheus HTTP API as tasks
(<https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/api/>).

members.name: query
members.signature: static async query(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusQuerySettings], PrometheusQuerySettings]) -> object
members.doc:
Evaluate an instant query (`/api/v1/query`).

``ts
const result = await PrometheusTasks.query((s) =>
  s.url("https://prometheus.internal").bearerToken(token)
    .query('sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m]))')
);
``

members.name: query_range
members.signature: static async query_range(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusQueryRangeSettings], PrometheusQueryRangeSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Evaluate a range query (`/api/v1/query_range`); the answer is a matrix.

members.name: series
members.signature: static async series(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusSeriesSettings], PrometheusSeriesSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Find the series matching selectors (`/api/v1/series`).

members.name: labels
members.signature: static async labels(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusLabelsSettings], PrometheusLabelsSettings]) -> object
members.doc: List label names (`/api/v1/labels`).

members.name: label_values
members.signature: static async label_values(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusLabelValuesSettings], PrometheusLabelValuesSettings]) -> object
members.doc: List one label's values (`/api/v1/label/<label_name>/values`).

members.name: metadata
members.signature: static async metadata(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusMetadataSettings], PrometheusMetadataSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read metric metadata (`/api/v1/metadata`), keyed by metric name.

members.name: targets
members.signature: static async targets(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusTargetsSettings], PrometheusTargetsSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read target discovery state (`/api/v1/targets`).

members.name: rules
members.signature: static async rules(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusRulesSettings], PrometheusRulesSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read the loaded alerting and recording rules (`/api/v1/rules`).

members.name: alerts
members.signature: static async alerts(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusConnectionSettings], PrometheusConnectionSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read the active alerts (`/api/v1/alerts`).

members.name: build_info
members.signature: static async build_info(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusConnectionSettings], PrometheusConnectionSettings]) -> object
members.doc: Read the server's build information (`/api/v1/status/buildinfo`).

members.name: healthy
members.signature: static async healthy(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusConnectionSettings], PrometheusConnectionSettings]) -> object
members.doc:
Probe `/-/healthy`: `true` on 2xx, `false` on 503, and a
`PrometheusApiError` on any other status — a 401 is a credential
problem, not an unhealthy server.

members.name: ready
members.signature: static async ready(ctx: ServiceContext, configure: Callable[[PrometheusConnectionSettings], PrometheusConnectionSettings]) -> object
members.doc:
Probe `/-/ready`: `true` once the server serves queries, `false` while it
answers 503, and a `PrometheusApiError` on any other status.

members.name: value
members.signature: static async value(ctx: ServiceContext, response: Mapping[str, object]) -> object
members.doc:
The single number an instant query returned — a scalar, or a vector of
exactly one float sample — failing clearly on an empty or multi-sample
vector, a matrix, a string or a native histogram. `NaN` is returned as
`NaN`, which compares false both ways — gate with `!(v <= max)`.

``ts
const ratio = PrometheusTasks.value(await PrometheusTasks.query((s) => …));
``

members.name: samples
members.signature: static async samples(ctx: ServiceContext, response: Mapping[str, object]) -> object
members.doc:
Every float sample of an instant query, with its labels: a vector's
elements, or a scalar as one unlabelled sample. An empty vector is an
empty list; a matrix, string or native histogram fails.

packages.name: zuke.tools.qr
packages.summary: `@zuke/qr` 1.2.0: `@zuke/qr` — QR codes for any data, from a Zuke build, with no dependency.

symbols.name: QrSettings
symbols.doc:
Configuration for encoding and rendering a QR code, set through a lambda
passed to a `QrTasks` method. Every setter returns `this` so calls chain.

members.name: error_correction
members.doc: Set the error-correction level: `"L"` (~7%), `"M"` (~15%), `"Q"` (~25%) or `"H"` (~30%).

members.name: boost_error_correction
members.doc:
Whether to raise the error-correction level when a higher one fits the
same version. On by default; turn it off to get exactly the level asked for.

members.name: quiet_zone
members.doc: Set the width of the light border around the symbol, in modules (0 to MAX_QUIET_ZONE).

members.name: invert

members.name: log_opts
members.doc:
Restrict which commits are scanned, passed straight through to `git log`
(`--log-opts`).

Without this, `gitleaks detect` walks the whole history reachable from the
refs present in the checkout — so on a pull request, where CI typically
fetches every branch, a secret-shaped string on an unrelated branch fails
the scan and the failure appears on whichever pull request is looked at.
Passing a range such as `origin/main..HEAD` scopes the scan to the commits
under review.

Has no effect alongside noGit, which makes gitleaks treat the
source as a plain directory and ignore history entirely.
